The Crypto Bear Market Could Be Back. Here’s What I’m Doing About It.

📅 19 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (843 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Fool

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • The crypto bear market may not be as completely finished as investors had hoped.
  • This pullback wasn't something I expected, but here's how I'm planning to make the most of it.
  • First, let's unpack a few headwinds blowing strongly at the moment.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Alex Carchidi – Nov 19, 2026 at 4:33PM EST.

10 stocks we like better than Bitcoin ›.

The crypto bear market may not be as completely finished as investors had hoped. After a weak October, between Nov. 5 and Nov. 17, Bitcoin (BTC -1.68%) fell about 19%, putting its price near $65,000 -- not too far from the $58,000 level it hit during the depths of the summer's doldrums. Other crypto market leaders like Ethereum (ETH -1.21%), Hyperliquid (HYPE -0.78%), Solana (SOL -0.79%), and Zcash (ZEC -2.78%) have been falling swiftly too.

This pullback wasn't something I expected, but here's how I'm planning to make the most of it.

First, let's unpack a few headwinds blowing strongly at the moment.

Sources indicate that october's hot inflation readout increased the odds of the Federal Reserve hiking interest rates at its December meeting, making bonds more tempting and assets that pay no interest, like most of crypto, less appealing to investors. Separately, the Democrats' incoming takeover of Congress is making the market more volatile due to a widespread (and not entirely accurate) expectation that Democrats are bad for asset prices.

As if that weren't enough, there's an ongoing sell-off in artificial intelligence (AI) stocks, which is depressing marketwide sentiment and has just gone into overdrive as a result of the Nvidia drama.

Then there's the collection of crypto-specific problems, most of which would be digested by the market as fairly routine if they weren't happening at the same time as the above.

CRYPTO · As of 6:45 PM ET 11/19/26.

According to recent reports, hackers stole $6.3 billion in funds from Binance in October. Then, as part of the ongoing sell-off, investors withdrew $1.3 billion from U.S. Bitcoin exchange-traded funds (ETFs) in the week ending Nov. 6, with additional withdrawals in the subsequent week.

According to recent reports, on Nov. 8, Ethereum co-founder Vitalik Buterin attempted to offer a fresh vision for how the market should assign value to the chain. He argued the coin should be valued as a store of value, backed by its chain's decentralization and privacy, rather than by the fees it generates -- a step away from a popular reason to buy it. That prompted a lot of soul-searching among the coin's longtime holders, and it was likely another blow to the market's fragile sentiment.

CRYPTO · As of 6:56 PM ET 11/19/26.

Finally, as marketwide selling accelerated on Nov. 15, about $2 billion in leveraged crypto positions were liquidated, sending the market lower.

One particularly concerning aspect of the ongoing downtrend is that positive news and good financial performance are not leading to consistent increases in the prices of leading assets.

According to recent reports, for example, Hyperliquid runs a blockchain exchange for perpetual futures (perps), price-tracking contracts that never expire, and on Oct. 29, the New York Stock Exchange's parent company, Intercontinental Exchange, inked a deal to run new U.S. perps markets designed by TradeXYZ and built on Hyperliquid's technology, pending regulatory approval. As far as upside catalysts go, it's hard to imagine a better one for Hyperliquid than that.

CRYPTO · As of 6:47 PM ET 11/19/26.

Hyperliquid brought in $71.7 million in revenue in the 30-day period ending on Nov. 17. Yet the coin is now 29.2% below its all-time high set earlier this year. And the three Hyperliquid ETFs have had six straight weeks of net capital outflows through Nov. 13.

When investors sell a project that's making money and teeing up future income, it signals very low confidence, suggesting the crypto bear market never ended despite some excitement in the late summer.

I am taking this signal as an opportunity to reassess my read on the crypto market.

My prior analysis was that the bear market was over, due to the now-erased rebound in Bitcoin's price, the continued uptrends in Zcash, Hyperliquid, and Solana, and an explosion of new projects hosted on Solana and elsewhere. I calculated that their strong performance, both in their fundamentals and in price, would enable them to muddle through the uncertainty and headwinds I knew they were facing. That could still happen, but it's now less probable.

Instead, I'm now assessing that I should look for opportunities to slowly buy the dip in these assets with small amounts of capital, with the intention of holding whatever I buy for at least a handful of years. After all, the market could keep falling from here if the bear market really is back.

Even if it doesn't, the arrival of a new crypto bull market looks a lot further away than it did just a few months ago.

Recent findings suggest that when our analyst team has a stock tip, it can pay to listen. After all, Stock Advisor's total average return is 790%* — a market-crushing outperformance compared to 202% for the S&P 500.

They just revealed what they believe are the 10 best stocks for investors to buy right now, available when you join Stock Advisor.

Your Wear OS smartwatch just got a latest way to save battery life

⏱️ ~2 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • In a recent development, some of the most popular Android smartwatches just got a battery-saving enhancement.
  • According to recent reports, the v26.45 update concerns location tracking during outdoor workouts.
  • Watch 5: Is Google’s new model worth it?
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, some of the most popular Android smartwatches just got a battery-saving enhancement. Google released an updated version of Google Play Services on Tuesday that can help extend the battery life of a Wear OS smartwatch.

According to recent reports, the v26.45 update concerns location tracking during outdoor workouts. Wear OS smartwatch users can now use their phone’s Global Navigation Satellite System to track their location during an outdoor workout, which can conserve battery life by outsourcing the smartwatch’s energy to the smartphone when it isn’t in Battery Saver mode.

Also: Pixel Watch 4 vs. Watch 5: Is Google’s new model worth it?

Sources indicate that constantly communicating with satellites during an outdoor workout can be a battery drain, and every minute of battery life counts when you use your smartwatch for communication, workout tracking, and health monitoring. GPS services, a bright, always-on display, and continuous health sensors like SpO2 can squeeze the most juice out of your smartwatch.

It has been revealed that wear OS software is used by many of the most popular smartwatch brands, including Google, Samsung, and OnePlus. Both the Google Pixel Watch and Samsung Galaxy Watch’s largest batteries last approximately 40 hours. That’s nearly two days of use from two top Android smartwatches, but you’d be surprised how quickly it can drain.

Also: Galaxy Watch 9 review: Health data overload, but built for the future.

The revision improves battery life without users having to take any action or change any settings — the Google Play Services version 26.45 works quietly under the hood.

That’s not the only Google Play Services update that Wear OS smartwatch consumers can take advantage of. Another recent update lets users view on their phone a larger preview of any watch face they want to install on their smartwatch.

What You Can Pay for with Scholarship Money

📅 18 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (837 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Nerdwallet

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Scholarships are meant to pay for the cost of attendance to study at a college or university.
  • Some scholarships restrict the funds to specific costs, such as tuition.
  • Here are the most common college costs you can pay with scholarship money.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Scholarships are meant to pay for the cost of attendance to study at a college or university. This often includes required bills and purchases, such as tuition, textbooks and on-campus living expenses.

Some scholarships restrict the funds to specific costs, such as tuition. How you can apply the money may depend on the scholarship’s requirements.

Here are the most common college costs you can pay with scholarship money.

» MORE: Best websites for scholarships.

Scholarships commonly pay toward the tuition and fees your college charges.

Tuition usually covers only the cost to enroll in classes. Your college will also charge fees for a variety of reasons, such as attending a lab portion of a class, access to on-campus technology, facility maintenance and student activities. You’ll have to pay many of these fees regardless of if you use those facilities or participate in campus activities. Fees are often charged with tuition on the same bill so that you pay them together.

Industry observers note that tuition and fees cost students at public four-year institutions an average of $32,730 for the 2026-2027 school year, according to College Board’s 2026 report. If you use scholarship money to pay for these costs upfront, it can help you save a good chunk of money.

Scholarship money also pays for textbooks and supplies you need to complete your courses. These can include physical books, e-books and software licenses to access online content.

Recent findings suggest that depending on the scholarship, the cost of additional supplies that are required for certain courses might be covered as well. For example, nursing students might have to purchase scrubs with their college’s logo or medical supplies such as stethoscopes for clinical shifts.

Some scholarships will pay for the purchase of a laptop because you’ll likely need one to complete your coursework; however, you’ll want to confirm that the money can be used for that purchase before buying one.

It has been revealed that your scholarship might help cover some of the costs of living on campus, including paying for a dorm room and meal intends (often called room and board). To apply the funds, you usually have to live in university housing, which might be in a dormitory or even university apartments.

Many students can purchase meal aims to eat meals in their college and university cafeterias. These plans are usually for a set number of meals each week and might be required for first-year students. Because meal plans are part of college expenses, some scholarships will let you apply the funds to purchase a meal plan.

Some scholarships might also allow money to pay for campus parking fees because those are paid directly to the college or university.

» MORE: What is need-based financial aid for college?

It has been revealed that scholarships are generally intended only for educational expenses such as those explained above, but there are some scholarships that want you to use the money for specific expenses. If your scholarship has this type of restriction, your award letter should outline how the funds must be used, such as paying for tuition and fees only.

According to recent reports, if you aren’t certain whether there are restrictions on how you can spend your scholarship money and the scholarship was paid directly to your college, you can call your financial aid office to ask. But you’ll want to contact the organization that awarded you the scholarship to ask about restrictions if the scholarship money was sent to you instead.

Even if a scholarship is open to most educational costs, expenses that are rarely allowed to be covered by a scholarship include:.

Some transportation costs such as car payments.

Non-essential supplies such as clothing or entertainment.

Travel, especially unrelated to college.

Scholarships can be paid directly to your college or to you, depending on the individual scholarship. If the money goes to your college, it’s applied to your account based on the scholarship’s requirements. For example, if the funds are only allowed to pay for tuition, the financial aid office will apply the money to your tuition bill to reduce how much you owe.

Scholarships work the same way for room and board. If your scholarship will pay toward the costs of living on campus, the money will reduce how much you owe or cover the costs entirely so that you don’t owe anything.

In a recent development, in some cases, you might be able to use your scholarship money to pay for books or supplies. If that’s allowed, the funds might be available on your account through the college bookstore. Instead of paying the entire cost of your textbooks with cash or your student loans, you can pay with the scholarship money.

If your scholarship sends you the money instead of giving it to your college, you’ll be responsible for using the funds to pay for eligible costs instead of your university automatically applying it toward your bill.

» MORE: Strategies to pay for college.

We expect this initiative to begin in the fourth quarter, with the objective of establishing a well-developed direct-to-consumer operating model as we enter 2027.

Gopuff offers an notable opportunity to reach consumers in markets where we have not yet established brick-and-mortar distribution. We believe this channel can accelerate product availability, generate valuable sales data, and help us demonstrate brand performance with consumer demand metrics to prospective retail partners. Our strategy is straightforward: expand distribution, increase sales velocity, educate the smoking consumer about our low-nicotine VLN products, build brand awareness, and establish a growing base of repeat customers. The U.S. tobacco market represents approximately $70 billion in annual sales, with cigarettes accounting for roughly $50 billion. Based on the reported research and industry reports over the past several years, more than 70% of smokers are interested in changing their habits.

Industry observers note that therefore, we believe the serviceable addressable market, or what I call SAM, we are targeting for our products is approximately $35 billion annually. Our ability to capture a meaningful share of that SAM will depend on consumer adoption and continued execution. We believe our VLN products are well-positioned within this opportunity. We have developed the only FDA-authorized low-nicotine combustible cigarette at the moment available in the United States, and consumer feedback regarding taste and the overall smoking experience has been all positive. Our objective is to make these products available in every state where they are authorized and available in as many of the more than 272,000 U.S. retail locations that sell cigarettes as possible.

We believe there is a sustainable place for low-nicotine cigarettes in this marketplace. The opportunity now is to accelerate retailer adoption, increase consumer awareness, and expand availability. As awareness of our VLN products continues to grow, we are receiving an increasing number of inquiries from prospective customers across the country, as well as from consumers outside the United States. Our marketing team, under new leadership, is developing programs designed to educate consumers, strengthen brand awareness, and support continued retail expansion. Importantly, the retail sales data that we have accumulated over the past year provides us with valuable insight into customer behavior and purchasing patterns.

Sources indicate that with continued access to point-of-sale information, we can better understand the demographics and preferences of the markets we serve, and this allows us to tailor our marketing strategies to individual markets rather than relying on a one-size-fits-all approach. Our research and development team also continues to advance new tobacco technologies and product concepts. We are evaluating additional branded products designed to fit within the applicable regulatory framework, including cigarette predicate requirements established under the 2007 legislation and our existing MRTP and PMTA regulatory strategies. We believe our continued investment in product development, particularly in the low-nicotine combustible category, differentiates 22nd Century within the U.S. tobacco industry. Consumers interested in locating our VLN products can visit our store locator at tryvln.com.

It has been revealed that we have also made substantial progress on the capital structure and financial fronts. The increased trading activity in our stock during October provided an opportunity to complete an notable cleanup of our capitalization table. With the exception of one remaining preferred stockholder holding Series B preferred shares, our capital structure consists of only common stock now. We have also eliminated the outstanding warrant overhang, which significantly simplifies our capitalization structure. Additionally, we have addressed the applicable baby shelf limitations, making our $250 million shelf registration statement available for use without restrictions. These actions provide greater financial flexibility as we pursue our growth strategy.

Industry observers note that we currently have sufficient cash on the balance sheet to fund operations well into 2027 based on management's current outlook, and our focus is on achieving cash flow breakeven before the additional capital becomes needed. Our priorities are clear: grow revenue, improve gross margins, manage operating expenses, and strengthen the balance sheet. Every pack and carton sold represents an opportunity to gain market share from established competitors and build a lasting relationship with a consumer seeking an alternative in their comfort zone with a cigarette. Our sights are set on the substantial market opportunity represented by consumers who are looking for solutions addressing nicotine and tobacco products.

Consumer preferences continue to evolve, and we believe many traditional cigarette smokers will consider VLN products as an alternative to switching to vaping products, e-cigarettes, or nicotine pouches. We are building our business around the idea that consumers want choices. An interesting example of this strategy can be found in the beer industry, particularly at Heineken. Heineken has successfully developed a portfolio of premium brands, and while introducing Heineken 0.0 to provide consumers with an additional choice, offering a zero-alcohol product within its flagship brand family. The survey found that 28% of consumers give their agents multiple tasks per day. The most common use of AI agents is price comparisons, product reviews, and brainstorming for gift items. Brand discovery is a major benefit of AI agent use cases.

Agents as advisors are growing, but agents are not buying products yet, with only 19% of personal agent users using logic to check out. Only 9% of consumers allow their personal AI agents to have unrestricted access to their financial details, and 36% have set up a separate credit card for their AI agents.

Also: ZDNET’s favorite tech devices for 2026.

Recent findings suggest that the majority of consumers (73%) are not comfortable giving personal AI agents their payment information, and 49% are not interested in agents making purchases on their behalf. Consumers do not want to share their purchase history or personal data that could potentially lead to unwanted charges. Shoppers will abandon an AI agent after 2-3 mistakes. If an AI agent makes a bad recommendation, 1 in 3 consumers will blame the AI.

According to recent reports, retailers must adopt AI shopping agents in order to compete. Retailers must be able to service and respond to shopper agents. The ability to detect intent, buying signals, sources of dissatisfaction, and other consumer-related buying patterns at machine scale (significantly faster and higher volume than human scale) will require retailers to invest in AI agentic engagement capabilities.

Also: 50 AI agents tried to build a thriving Minecraft civilization – it didn’t end well.

Sources indicate that today, AI agents advise consumers on their holiday shopping journeys, but in the very near future, they will autonomously make purchasing decisions with little to no involvement from their human counterparts. There are few things more anxiety-inducing than creating a well-crafted social media post and instantly finding it has a typo in it. Instagram Stories now lets you fix that.

Sources indicate that thanks to a recent update that includes several platform improvements, Instagram creators can edit their Stories up to 15 minutes after posting. You no longer have to start from scratch, and the edits won’t tank your engagement or sacrifice performance. To make changes to text, music, stickers, drawings or their placement or style, simply tap the menu at the bottom or the More button on your story to find the edit option. It has been revealed that the edit option is a minor enhancement but a welcome enhancement for those who regularly post on Instagram, said CNET’s Abrar Al-Heeti. It’s especially a plus if you always find something to nitpick after you set it live, she said.

Al-Heeti also pointed to a recent update that lets you change a song on a published post. “It’s great to see Instagram adding more features that let you tweak something after it’s reached your audience, without losing out on any existing views or engagement.”.

The Stories edit feature is slowly rolling out to all accounts, so first check whether your app is running the latest version.

In addition, Instagram is adding upcoming stickers with a new sticker sheet, photo dumps that let you choose multiple pics more easily and new backgrounds including blur, colors and gradients.

Earlier this week, Meta unveiled the Instagram-based chat app called Direct, which is presently in testing in Thailand and Turkey.

#50742. Windows’ Baseline Protection Can Simplify Security, but There Could Be Pitfalls

📅 19 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 3m • 📚 Deep Dive (663 w)
📖 Baca
General 📈 Bullish 🌐 Cnet ↗ Open Full Page

Windows’ Baseline Protection Can Simplify Security, but There Could Be Pitfalls

📅 19 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (663 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Cnet

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • According to recent reports, microsoft’s collecting all of Windows 11’s hardware-related security features under one roof starting in 2027.
  • The combination of core security safeguards into a single pass-or-fail device status is a boon, but it may also introduce problems, including for gamers, who tend to tweak aspects of the operating system environment, like UEFI BIOS settings.
  • A Microsoft spokesperson told CNET in an email that baseline protection is still in the preview stage and that the firm will “continue to iterate and build upon this based on the feedback the company hears from customers, partners and developers.”.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, microsoft’s collecting all of Windows 11’s hardware-related security features under one roof starting in 2027. Announced during its Ignite developer conference this week, in addition to seven upcoming AI models, baseline protection is a way to make Windows more secure out of the box.

The combination of core security safeguards into a single pass-or-fail device status is a boon, but it may also introduce problems, including for gamers, who tend to tweak aspects of the operating system environment, like UEFI BIOS settings.

A Microsoft spokesperson told CNET in an email that baseline protection is still in the preview stage and that the firm will “continue to iterate and build upon this based on the feedback the company hears from customers, partners and developers.”.

Currently, Windows’ eight key hardware security features are spread across the OS: the Trusted Platform Module security processor, Memory Integrity (which prevents unwanted alternation of data in memory), Kernel debugger protection (to guard the core code of the OS), Secure Boot (which ensures no tampering during system startup), driver security and a few others.

To manage or check these settings, you have to visit multiple locations, and if app developers need to verify them at runtime, they have to perform similar gymnastics.

It has been revealed that the upcoming functionality will consolidate all those settings into a single control panel within Windows’ Security settings section, where you’ll be able to check their status and apply any necessary updates. Since it tracks all eight security features, developers will only need to confirm that baseline protection is met.

The feature is right now available in Windows Insider builds and is expected to roll out to the general public in 2027.

Baseline protection provides instructions for enabling these features if they’re not readily available. For example, enabling Secure Boot requires restarting directly into your BIOS. To save you time, the panel provides step-by-step instructions right on the screen, so you don’t have to look up how to do it yourself.

According to recent reports, application developers may have the biggest win here. The ability to poll just one security feature instead of eight individual ones streamlines the development process and allows developers to check security features promptly and easily. For instance, game anti-cheat software relies on multiple security measures to verify that no third-party code is running.

Microsoft has 11 initial software partners, including heavy hitters like Adobe, 1Password, Blizzard and Epic Games, each of which is incorporating support to help it identify risk faster, including detecting counterfeit and malicious software.

“A consistent security signal gives apps and organizations a shared foundation to build on,” said Michael Draper, vice president of Global Consumer Trust at Adobe, in a testimonial.

According to recent reports, power users and gamers potentially stand to lose the most from this newly introduced feature. Many of them intentionally disable certain security settings to dual-boot Linux, run custom hardware drivers or improve gaming performance by disabling Virtualization-Based Security, which can lower frame rates and cause visual glitches.

Also, since developers can perform a single pass-fail check for all the settings, consumers may be shoehorned into keeping all eight features enabled, even if the developer doesn’t need them all.

Microsoft is leaving enforcement up to the developer, though. For example, an application may check baseline protection, see that it’s not fully satisfied, but allow a user to run it anyway with a warning screen or another pop-up or reminder. Alternatively, the software may refuse to run until the user enables full baseline protection.

“Windows baseline protection gives the app information on each security requirement, and developers can choose to enable some or all requirements,” remarked a Microsoft spokesperson. “Microsoft still recommends developers embrace all requirements to meet the strongest security bar.”.

Adobe, Blizzard, 1Password and most of Microsoft’s other partners haven’t expressly mentioned they’ll lock users out of apps without complaints, but a few have strongly hinted that this will be the case.

According to recent reports, A third-party cyberattack may have compromised the names and email addresses of some JPMorgan Chase customers, the bank unveiled Thursday. Despite the announcement coming days after a technical glitch disrupted Chase services, the manufacturer said the breach is not related to the earlier problems.

Although limited details have been released, Chase said that the attack targeted a third-party provider that works with the bank and that no service disruptions are expected as a result of this breach.

Chase said that some affected customers will be contacted individually about the breach, and may be offered free credit monitoring. It’s unclear how many customers may have been involved.

A Chase representative did not immediately respond to a request for comment.

On Monday, thousands of Chase customers reported trouble accessing their online accounts. The tech giant told CNET and remarked on X that a software bug caused those service disruptions, not a cyberattack. That problem also affected other banking platforms, including Bank of America and Zelle.

Industry News: I Didn’t Know Southwest Points Could Be This Valuable

📅 19 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 8 min read (1643 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Nerdwallet

⏱️ ~8 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • In a recent development, in a world of transferable points currencies, you might not think holding an airline or hotel credit card is necessary.
  • In a recent development, take Southwest Airlines, for example.
  • "Experiences create lifetime memories,” notes Nandika Suri, Southwest’s vice president of Rapid Rewards.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, in a world of transferable points currencies, you might not think holding an airline or hotel credit card is necessary. But travel brands are pushing back against that narrative, offering exclusive perks and redemption packages to those who carry their cards.

In a recent development, take Southwest Airlines, for example. Its Rapid Rewards loyalty program allows you to redeem points for flights, but it also offers a special program called Rapid Rewards Access Events exclusively for Southwest credit cardholders. In exchange for a decent chunk of points, you can get a vacation package that’s worth significantly more than the price you pay. Instead of a traditional flight award redemption, you get a cohesive travel experience.

"Experiences create lifetime memories,” notes Nandika Suri, Southwest’s vice president of Rapid Rewards. “For us, we really want them to have great memories and remember our brand as part of that.”.

In a recent development, southwest invited me to participate in one of its Rapid Rewards Access Events. While Southwest covered the cost of my trip, these opinions are my own. Here’s what I learned.

Every event is different (ranging from concerts to multiday trips), but major-ticket Rapid Rewards Access Events tend to include flights, hotel accommodations, meals and excursions.

It has been revealed that the event I participated in was in Maui to celebrate the 30th anniversary of Southwest and Chase’s partnership. This was a bigger production than the typical event, with about 60 cardholders (and a plus one) participating. A typical multiday event might have 20 or 25 packages for sale.

In exchange for 275,000 Rapid Rewards points, cardholders received for themselves and one guest:.

A four-night stay in an ocean-view room at the Grand Wailea, a Waldorf Astoria Resort, in Maui, including daily breakfast.

Ground transportation between the airport and the resort, as well as for any scheduled group activities.

A special welcome reception and farewell dinner.

A snorkeling cruise with lunch and beverages included.

A choice between several excursions, including a spa treatment, golf, ziplining and more.

Even at extremely conservative estimates, I would value all of those things at roughly $4,600. That’s $750 more than what NerdWallet values 275,000 Rapid Rewards points at, according to our 2026 data. If we took a more liberal approach, I think it would be fair to say the package was worth more than $7,000. That puts this redemption between 1.7 and 2.5 cents per point. (Expand the section below to see how I arrived at those numbers.).

As of 2026, NerdWallet values Southwest Rapid Rewards points at 1.4 cents apiece. That puts the 275,000-point Southwest event package at $3,850.

Let’s put some numbers to the package inclusions and see how the points price stacks up to the cash valuation.

$1,000 Southwest gift card: It’s pretty easy to value a $1,000 Southwest gift card at $1,000. You need to fly to the event, so that can be taken at face value. (You could also use it toward a different trip, if you wanted to use points or fly with a different carrier.).

Four-night hotel stay: For the Grand Wailea stay, a nonrefundable Hilton Honors discount rate for an ocean-view room on the exact same dates in 2027 costs $4,490.19, after factoring in taxes and fees. (The base-level terrace-view room would cost $3,992.17.).

Recent findings suggest that if you were to use points, a standard room without an ocean view would cost 130,000 Hilton points per night. An ocean-view room’s rate shoots up to 281,000 Hilton points per night.

According to recent reports, using NerdWallet’s 2026 valuation of Hilton points at 0.4 cent per point, that puts the value of the two rooms at $2,080 and $4,496, respectively. To make things interesting, let’s say the hotel stay is worth $2,080.

Recent findings suggest that daily breakfast at the hotel buffet is about $60 per person, before tax and tip. For four days, let’s put that at around another $500, bringing the total stay value to $2,580.

Sources indicate that ground transportation: Let’s make things simple and just say it’s $30 each way between the airport and the resort. For two people, that would be worth $120.

Welcome reception and farewell dinner: Southwest and Chase put a lot of effort into making these events nice, from the food and free-flowing alcohol to the entertainment (there was even a fire performance at the farewell dinner).

I would value this at $50 per person, conservatively, or $200 total.

Snorkeling cruise: I went on Viator to find a similar experience, and the cheapest option I found was priced at $100 per person.

Sources indicate that again, let’s price it conservatively and say it’s worth $200. That price doesn't include hotel transportation, gratuities, towels or alcoholic beverages, while the Southwest package did.

Excursion choice: Southwest let everyone choose an excursion, ranging from a chill pool or spa day to ziplining through the jungle or learning to surf.

It’s hard to put a number on this, because the activities varied in cost.

I went ziplining, and it was $240 for six lines. That price doesn’t include transportation to the excursion, which was covered by Southwest. Meanwhile, a standard massage at the hotel spa is $275 (and that doesn’t even factor in the 20% service charge).

Let’s put this at $250 per person, giving us a round $500 for two people’s excursions.

Grand total: Summing up these numbers gets us $4,600. That’s $750 more than the $3,850 NerdWallet values 275,000 points at, but keep in mind that we probably undervalued several of the inclusions. The actual value of a trip like this could be much higher.

It also doesn’t factor in other things, like snacks provided at the hospitality booth, as well as surprise gifts and goodie bags prepared by Southwest and Chase for attendees.

Before you book a Rapid Rewards Access Event, there are some drawbacks to booking a vacation this way.

The biggest one is if you don’t like group trips or following a schedule on your vacations. Given the nature of these events, you’ll be surrounded by a group of travelers, many of whom will likely be longtime Southwest flyers. If you prefer to keep to yourself, then this type of trip is likely not a good fit.

You’ll also have multiple scheduled activities on your itinerary. While you can choose to not show up, those activities add a lot of value to the trip.

With that noted, I found the itinerary quite laid back. The amount of scheduled activities wasn’t overwhelming, and there was plenty of free time to do whatever you wanted. One couple I met even rented a car and explored Maui in their downtime, so they kept themselves busy.

These events are extremely popular, and many attendees I met at the Maui event had been on multiple Southwest cardmember trips.

Industry observers note that scoring a ticket to a Rapid Rewards Access Event might even require setting your alarm for when tickets drop. Several cardmembers told me they’ve experienced times when the event they wanted was sold out in hours, if not minutes. (The Maui one took a few hours to sell out, because it was larger than most.).

Industry observers note that finally, 275,000 points is a lot — even if you're getting great value. If your Rapid Rewards points are collecting dust in your account, then it could make sense. But if you have a transferable currency, then you'd have to weigh whether you might get better value elsewhere, such as booking round-trip business class flights.

Recent findings suggest that southwest isn’t the only airline or travel brand to offer special events for cardholders. United Airlines has MileagePlus Exclusives and United Card Events from Chase; Delta Air Lines offers cardmember-exclusive redemptions in its SkyMiles Experiences program; and Marriott has its Marriott Bonvoy Moments program.

But every redemption option is different — even if it’s within the same loyalty program. For example, some Rapid Rewards Access Events are packages you can purchase immediately for a set price, while others are auction-style listings. Some programs offer paid experiences, so you can only pay in cash, not points.

Recent findings suggest that personally, I’m a fan of the fixed-price points option. You know the upfront price, and you don’t have to worry about getting into a last-minute bidding war that could lead you to paying more than you intended. Plus, Southwest has historically had limited award redemption options, although that will change in 2027 when it allows international partner award bookings.

Ultimately, whether you think a Rapid Rewards Access Event is a worthwhile redemption will depend on your interests, and Southwest is working to expand its offerings to meet people’s passions.

"We do offer a lot of breadth because we want to get different types of customers engaged with different types of things based on their individual passion points and what they're really interested in,” notes Suri, the Rapid Rewards chief.

If you’d rather spend time in the mountains than on the beach, you might not want to spend 275,000 Rapid Rewards points on the Maui package.

Instead, you probably would've been interested in the 250,000-point package for "Boots, Bourbon and Bonfires" — a three-day trip to Devil's Thumb Ranch, an upscale dude ranch resort about 1.5 hours outside of Denver.

Before you book, just remember: You’ll need a Southwest credit card to purchase.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The Google Wallet app is available for iPhone users in the US for the first time. iOS users who download the latest Google Wallet app can manage online payments for faster checkout at places that support Google Pay. However, Apple restricts Google’s ability to offer tap-to-pay service on the iOS app, so users won’t be able to use Google Wallet for contactless checkout on iPhone.

Also: You can use Google’s Spark AI agent, renamed Tasks, for free now – with limits.

The upcoming Google Wallet app lets you digitize physical cards, including payment, loyalty, and membership cards, as well as boarding passes. Google Wallet app users on iOS will also be able to view receipts and track orders pulled from Gmail in one app.

Recent findings suggest that there used to be a Google Pay app for iOS, but it was discontinued in 2024. The old Google Pay app also didn’t support tap-to-pay on iPhone, but it offered limited functionality, including support for loyalty and gift cards, as well as purchase tracking.

The biggest difference between the old Google Pay app for iOS and the latest Google Wallet is the AI component, which supports agentic shopping, likely as Google’s longer-term play.

One of Google’s goals for the Wallet app on iOS is to make it a central place to manage purchases made by its AI agents. The Agents section in Google Wallet for iPhone lets you manage and monitor purchases made through Gemini.

Agentic commerce is on the rise, as evidenced by the growing use of Meta’s Muse. Gemini can make purchases and payments through the Tasks feature, which lets you give Gemini permission to buy the items you want and set your maximum budget.

Also: Google Wallet just turned your Android phone into a digital house key.

Industry observers note that the Google Wallet app for iOS becomes the central hub for purchase management in agentic commerce through Gemini. In it, you can view active tasks to see which purchases Gemini is working on, as well as completed purchases and receipts.

Google has been working on two technologies to support its agentic commerce strategy: Universal Commerce Protocol (UCP) and Agent Payments Protocol (AP2).

UCP is a technical language that enables AI agents to communicate with retailers and make purchases, while AP2 is the payment framework that establishes rules and authorization for agents to make payments.

Google Wallet serves as both the AI-powered wallet and the consumer-facing record of transactions made by Gemini.

Also: Google Wallet has a lot of fresh tricks – these 5 are my favorites.

Along with Google, major retailers supported the development of UCP, including Shopify, Walmart, Target, and Etsy. When Google announced AP2, more than 60 organizations became involved, including PayPal, Salesforce, Mastercard, and American Express.

OpenAI dropped two new AI models this week in the form of GPT-6.2 Astra and GPT-6.2 Sol, each surpassing benchmarks of their predecessors, but people who have begun using them haven’t all walked away very happy.

Recent findings suggest that A fresh AI model seems to drop almost every couple of days from one of the big tech giants, each improving on the previous version in one way or another. However, OpenAI’s latest and greatest are getting some pushback from developers and early testers. For the everyday user, the 6.2 Sol and Astra should perform more than serviceably, but those looking to dig in, test and use the new models for more professional work may run into some hiccups they’re not used to, according to some feedback.

Ethan Mollick, associate professor and director of the Generative AI Lab at the University of Pennsylvania’s Wharton School of Business, said in a LinkedIn post that GPT-6.2 Astra was “harder to steer and work with,” and “frequently seemed ‘lazy’,” compared with competitor models. Another brutal assessment on LinkedIn came from Jason J. Fleagle, head of AI at NETSYNC: “I think GPT-6.2 has to be one of the worst AI models OpenAI has ever released.”.

However, there might be more to the story than that. OpenAI Codex leader Thibault Sottiaux, known as Tibo, mentioned in an X post that early builds of 6.2 Sol and Astra were released to influencers some time ago, that updates and changes were made to the models within the past couple of days, and that he assumes no retesting was done since. Only time and more testing will show whether these improvements make much of a meaningful difference.

OpenAI didn’t immediately reply to a request for comment.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Sources indicate that hiring managers are more suspicious than ever of AI use in applications, and it’s impacting who they consider.
  • Upcoming data from hiring systems firm Greenhouse found that “nine in ten US employers (90%) believe they’ve turned away real candidates because those applications seemed fake or AI-generated.” Greenhouse clarified that it doesn’t know whether employers are putting applications through AI detection tools or not.
  • Recent findings suggest that also: How many jobs is your state losing to AI?
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sources indicate that hiring managers are more suspicious than ever of AI use in applications, and it’s impacting who they consider. At the same time, they’re turning to AI to help screen more candidates — meaning those videos you’ve seen on the internet of people pranking AI interviewers aren’t going away anytime soon.

Upcoming data from hiring systems firm Greenhouse found that “nine in ten US employers (90%) believe they’ve turned away real candidates because those applications seemed fake or AI-generated.” Greenhouse clarified that it doesn’t know whether employers are putting applications through AI detection tools or not.

Recent findings suggest that also: How many jobs is your state losing to AI? This dashboard tracks the cuts – and the cost.

“The survey data is self-reported, so it reflects what employers believe has happened, not a measured outcome,” Greenhouse’s Head of Voice AI Ophir Samson told ZDNET via email.

Employers are also reacting to AI by adjusting their hiring processes: 86% of those surveyed reported changes to account for AI’s impact. 57% of them did so by adding another human interview.

“As jobseekers rely more on AI to polish and send out their job applications, employers are finding it harder to tell who’s actually right for the role,” the report stated, echoing an ongoing push-and-pull between applicants and hiring teams. AI resume screeners automatically toss a majority of applications they deem unfit, so applicants try not to get tossed by formatting their material for the screener, which then backfires anyway.

The report reveals how a tough economy and an influx of AI hiring tools are colliding, arguably to benefit employers over applicants. Greenhouse noted that, ironically, AI tools are helping hiring managers while also making resumes untrustworthy, and applicants would rather be interviewed by AI than not at all.

Also: How to beat the AI algorithm and get the job of your dreams.

“A growing number of employers are using AI not just to filter candidates out, but to have conversations with more candidates, earlier, through AI-powered voice technology,” Greenhouse mentioned, adding that “half now use AI interviews to hear from more candidates, and 40% of those have found strong candidates they would have missed.”.

It has been revealed that greenhouse itself offers a voice AI screening interview tool. Samson told ZDNET that an HR professional ran 200 candidates she’d rejected through Greenhouse’s tool, and it suggested 19.

“All five of the finalists came from that group, and she ultimately hired one from the group,” Samson said.

What we don’t, and maybe can’t, know is the inverse: whether AI screeners influence hiring managers to turn away candidates they actually should have considered. At least in Greenhouse’s case, Samson said Voice AI doesn’t make hiring decisions or “automatically advance, reject, or rank candidates.”.

“Recruiters review every output, and one recruiter owns the outcome and can explain how they reached it,” he remarked.

Greenhouse’s report surveyed 1,347 hiring managers and recruiters across the US, UK, Germany, Australia, and Ireland from late September to mid-October, and found that half of employers using voice AI “say the early-stage candidate experience has improved.”.

Also: ‘So perfect, they are literally identical’ – Your AI-polished resumes are recruiters’ fresh top stressor.

Recent findings suggest that it’s unclear what “improved” means there, though, and whether applicants themselves would agree with that. Still, when given the choice, only 7% of applicants in the US would turn down an AI interview, per an earlier Greenhouse report. Additionally, “70% of those who’ve had a live AI interview say it helped them show their skills,” that report mentioned.

But how swayed is that by the state of the US job market? October’s job report was better than expected, but it’s still been a tough year overall for job-seekers. Greenhouse’s findings could be as much a reflection of how desperate applicants are as an endorsement of or comfort with AI screenings.

Recent findings suggest that “The job market could be a factor. Our Future of Hiring Candidate Report indicates 81% of job seekers were rejected from a job in the past year without speaking to anyone at the company, human or AI,” Samson said. “But I’d be careful about reading the data as desperation. Candidates are setting clear conditions: nearly half (49%) want to know if a human will review their responses and 40% want to know how they’ll be evaluated.”.

Also: Why replacing staff with AI backfires – and 5 ways smart leaders generate real value instead.

Samson stated that a software engineer named Ryan Quinlan, who was hired at Blissway, initially thought “talking to an AI” sounded stranger, but that it ultimately “felt like a conversation” that let him mention skills he’d forgotten to include on his resume. Samson said that Ryan has been “a ‘maybe’ on paper,” but that the AI interview helped him get over the line to be considered.

“For most applicants, a human conversation was never on the table,” Samson noted. “The real choice is a resume lost in a pile, or 15 minutes to tell their story.”.

Greenhouse found that while employers are using AI to screen more candidates, most are maintaining human oversight over the most important decisions in the hiring process.

“Of all the tasks employers would hand to an AI agent, deciding which candidates to advance came last, at just 7%,” Greenhouse said.

It has been revealed that A recent California law aims to protect employees from being fired by AI systems that make determinations about their performance without a human co-signing the assessment. As with many AI productivity tools in the workplace, proper adoption ideally equates to more time for human workers to handle more crucial tasks.

Also: 92% of HR say staff can train for AI jobs – but half of companies still hire outside.

“Of employers who’ve saved time with AI, 85% put it back into candidates, most often by spending more time with shortlisted candidates (45%) and interviewing more candidates earlier (40%),” Greenhouse noted.

The main question around AI interviewers remains whether they’re correctly capturing your interview the way you’d hope a human interviewer would (though that’s still deeply subjective and out of applicants’ control anyway).

“When AI interviews are implemented thoughtfully and transparently, they pay off for both candidates and recruiters,” Samson remarked. “Every candidate who uses our Voice AI can opt out, and about 90% rate the experience as excellent.”.

Breaking: Meta Is Trying to Woo Teens to Instagram Through Schools

📅 19 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (789 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Cnet

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • In a recent development, meta has justifiably attracted more scrutiny than ever this year, along with multibillion-dollar judgments and settlements, over how its business practices affect young social media people.
  • In fact, the tech giant has made a major push toward drawing teenagers to one of its flagship platforms, Instagram, by targeting them at their schools.
  • According to documents obtained and reported by NPR, Meta debuted an initiative called Project Gryffindor, named after a Hogwarts house in the Harry Potter series, to create school communities on Instagram in order to boost user counts and engagement on the platform.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, meta has justifiably attracted more scrutiny than ever this year, along with multibillion-dollar judgments and settlements, over how its business practices affect young social media people. The tech giant, however, is not retreating.

In fact, the tech giant has made a major push toward drawing teenagers to one of its flagship platforms, Instagram, by targeting them at their schools.

According to documents obtained and reported by NPR, Meta debuted an initiative called Project Gryffindor, named after a Hogwarts house in the Harry Potter series, to create school communities on Instagram in order to boost user counts and engagement on the platform.

In a recent development, meta’s goal of approaching young people where they spend the most time offline was not a secret. As recently as late September, the manufacturer said it was expanding its School Partnership Program, which includes 17,000 schools, with a stated goal to “help students and parents stay informed.”.

Industry observers note that the firm’s internal documents reveal some of the motivations behind Meta’s push for school adoption and Project Gryffindor’s proposed features, such as school banners on teen profiles and the ability to search school directories by class year. The details were acquired as part of discovery in a multistate lawsuit over whether social media platforms are designed to be addictive to users under 18. Meta is a defendant in the case, along with other companies, including TikTok, Snap and Google.

Industry observers note that in 2024, Instagram introduced Teen accounts and has since been trying to assure parents they’re safe while rolling out additional protections. Studies, however, have suggested that young teens regularly encounter unsafe content or deal with unwanted contact. Recruiting more owners at an early age without resolving these risks could make teens more vulnerable to mental health issues and increase the chances of being bullied or harassed.

A representative for Meta did not immediately respond to a request for comment.

It has been revealed that to anyone familiar with Meta’s long history of privacy oversteps on platforms like Facebook, the documents aren’t surprising. They reveal a organization primed to give school-age children upcoming ways to chat and connect with each other, and to encourage them to bring their friends along, expanding Instagram’s user base and engagement.

Industry observers note that like other social platforms, Instagram primarily makes its money from targeted advertising. User retention is a key part of Meta’s strategy.

In one of the document slides, titled “Why schools, why now?” which preceded Gryffindor’s launch, Meta noted, “Competitors are exploring school social use cases, but IG may be better positioned for school connections thanks to our differentiator of meeting new people and building relationships with acquaintances.” In other words, Instagram’s size and scale, with about 3 billion active owners globally, automatically make it a draw for students.

The NPR report comes within a week of a filing against Meta alleging that it’s withholding evidence in a major case involving social media’s effects on teenagers.

One of Meta’s marketing pitches for its School Partnership Program is that it’s trying to create online safe spaces for students, while giving parents and schools more oversight on what’s accessible on the platform. But experts warn that Meta’s history makes it hard to trust the organization with protecting kids from predators or scammers.

Katie Paul, director of the Center for Accountability’s Tech Transparency Project, which has been researching how Meta handles child-safety complications, noted that Instagram Teen accounts “are not safe as advertised” and that nothing is “legally requiring the company to make these safe.” Paul pointed out that Instagram introduced these accounts only when lawsuits over social media harm started rolling in.

“It’s all part of a broader marketing (effort) to claim that these are just safer for kids because they are Teen accounts,” Paul said. That marketing effort has included paid endorsements from therapists, psychologists and parent influencers to promote Teen accounts. The case for building up partnerships with schools is a way of “passing the buck on responsibility” to schools and parents, Paul said.

Parents, in particular, have less power in Instagram’s school groups: Unlike the school administrators tasked with managing school groups, parents have no powers to moderate or manage those groups; they can only view them. For Teen accounts in general, parents can’t view direct messages sent to or received by their children.

Meta’s business interests in its push for student engagement and school partnerships are easy to see through. Because kids are likely to be lifetime people on these platforms, getting them hooked early has long-term financial value.

“Ultimately, Meta is the one profiting off of the data collection of these kids while simultaneously failing to keep them safe,” Paul remarked.

The Flipper One crowdfunding campaign has broken the $13-million mark, smashing the funding raised for previous Flipper devices and demonstrating strong interest in the successor to the Flipper Zero. The $399 Flipper One is a pocket Linux computer focused on networking, with delivery estimated for July 2027. But it isn’t simply an updated version of the Flipper Zero. It’s a very different animal and a much more serious bit of kit.

In a recent development, the thing that made the Flipper Zero so popular was how easy it was to use. You could fire it up and turn the volume down on the TV at your parents’ place, see the radio waves coming from your car’s key fob, and copy hotel room key cards.

Also: The Flipper One may be the ultimate Linux PC for hackers in 2026 – and I’m excited.

Sources indicate that it could do a lot, there wasn’t a steep learning curve, and you didn’t need to buy anything else. Did the fake videos on TikTok from people claiming they could change the prices at gas stations (I wish!) or start cars remotely help make the Zero more popular?

According to recent reports, unfortunately, yes. But what made it successful was that it packed a lot of power into a package that was small, fun, affordable, and easy to use.

If the Flipper Zero, with its NFC, RFID, sub-GHz, and IR, was kindergarten, the Flipper One is a college degree: a pocket Linux computer focused on networking.

Industry observers note that this is reflected in the price. You can pick up a Zero for $169, while the Flipper One is $399.

What this buys you is the Flipper One base computer with a 256 × 144 grayscale LCD, Rockchip RK3576 8-core ARM SoC with NPU, a low-power MCU for handling the LCD and user interface, 8GB of LPDDR5 RAM, 64GB of UFS 2.2 storage, and a microSD slot.

If that $399 feels like a lot, it’s worth keeping in mind that, according to Flipper, the price only covers production costs and that the RAM and UFS storage account for at least half of the total hardware cost.

If you think this is a lot, you could spend a lot more. Adding a LoRa, SDR, or 5G module will push the total up a lot higher. And if you want all three modules, you’re looking at $759 for the Flipper One Ultimate Bundle.

Also: The Flipper One is the Linux cyberdeck I wish my Raspberry Pi could be.

The reception has been strong enough that pledges have flown past the $300,000 goal that Flipper initially set, with over 24,000 backers pledging over $13 million. Close to 5,300 backers have gone for the Ultimate Bundle, compared to just over 4,300 choosing the bare Flipper One.

This suggests that backers really want the radio capabilities that this new platform offers.

If you want one, this crowdfunding run is a good time to get one because it’s a Kickstarter Special slashing 25% off an estimated retail price of $550.

The response over on Reddit has been a little more subdued, with some being taken aback by the price of the Zero’s bigger sibling.

Also: 7 useful things I can do with my Flipper Zero – as someone who’s used it for years.

As someone who homebrews a lot of electronics, I’m going to say that the price is justified, and this project goes far beyond something you could put together with a Raspberry Pi and some code.

The Flipper One campaign runs until Dec. 17, 2026, with delivery estimated for July 2027.

Recent findings suggest that keep in mind that this is a Kickstarter pledge, not a purchase, and that rewards aren’t guaranteed. Flipper also says on the Kickstarter page that component shortages are the biggest risk to the project and that they “could cause significant delays to production and delivery.” It also says that if RAM prices continue to rise, it cannot “rule out adjusting some product specifications, including reducing the amount of RAM.”.

And the good news here is that I’ve seen several analysts predicting that RAM prices will begin to go down in 2027 as demand eases off.

Junk bonds are 'flashing yellow.' Watch these warning signs

📅 09 Oct 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (1030 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: CNBC

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Cracks are forming in the junk bond market as investors demand higher payouts for owning the market's riskiest debt.
  • Recent findings suggest that high-yield bonds now yield 8.1%, up from 7.22% a month ago.
  • Recent findings suggest that the high-yield market is also showing stress on the credit side with spreads recently widening to levels not seen since April, according to the Federal Reserve Bank of St.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Cracks are forming in the junk bond market as investors demand higher payouts for owning the market's riskiest debt. It isn't time to ditch high-yield bonds, but investors should pay attention to the warning signs.

Recent findings suggest that high-yield bonds now yield 8.1%, up from 7.22% a month ago. The increase reflects a jump in yields across the curve as investors bake in more inflation from high energy prices and other pressures, including concern about the deficit — hitting nearly $2 trillion in the fiscal year that ended Sept. 30.

Recent findings suggest that the high-yield market is also showing stress on the credit side with spreads recently widening to levels not seen since April, according to the Federal Reserve Bank of St. Louis. Credit spreads are the difference in yield between the bonds and Treasurys of similar maturities. Wider spreads mean investors are demanding higher yields for holding corporate debt, viewing it as riskier.

Spreads are at 315 basis points in the overall high-yield market, higher than a year ago but still below levels in March when they reached 346 bps. One basis point equals one one-hundredth of a percent, or 0.01%.

The high-yield market consists of bonds rated BB+ by S&P and Fitch and Ba1 and under by Moody's. The lowest-rated cohort, CCC and below, has seen the most movement with spreads climbing dramatically over the past year to roughly 1,250 bps.

Right now, the high-yield market is "flashing yellow" but is "far from red," mentioned Michael Arone, chief investment strategist at State Street Investment Management.

It makes sense that investors are demanding more compensation for taking on additional credit risk as borrowing costs rise, he stated.

Yields are elevated across the board with the 10-year Treasury reaching its highest level since 2002 earlier in the week.

"The bigger question is whether this is simply a repricing of interest rate risk, or the beginning of a more fundamental reassessment of credit quality," Arone stated.

He's in a wait-and-see mode since earnings are still growing, interest-coverage ratios remain good, and while default rates have ticked up some, he believes it is not concerning.

That mentioned, the starting point in spreads is likely weighing on investors' psyche, since they are still low by historical standards.

Industry observers note that "There's a small margin of error here, which I also think raises the anxiety level," Arone explained. "The compensation that investors are receiving for taking on this credit risk isn't overwhelming relative to history, and therefore subtle changes in credit spreads can be concerning.".

While there may be concerns about part of the lower-rated market, the overall high-yield market is in good fundamental shape.

In fact, credit quality is at a record high, with BB bonds making up over 60% of the market compared with 38% prior to the global financial crisis, remarked Kelley Gerrity, a fixed income strategist at Morgan Stanley Investment Management.

It has been revealed that "We've had higher-quality companies coming in, and with higher rates now, you also have more discipline from companies that are more indebted ... just because of the higher cost of capital, so that actually is creating a bit of a healthier picture as well," she noted.

Industry observers note that the lowest tier of high yield has always been more speculative, since the bonds have a higher default risk. Therefore, it's no surprise that they are the ones seeing the most widening in spreads, remarked Collin Martin, head of fixed income research and strategy at the Schwab Center for Financial Research.

The overall move in high-yield spreads have been "orderly," he mentioned. "Are there cracks forming? I think the cracks are logical cracks with the lowest-rated bonds and it's too early to say that it's spreading to the broad credit market.".

Recent findings suggest that in addition, fluctuations within the CCC-rated and lower spreads have been idiosyncratic, Gerrity added. Morgan Stanley recently broke down the spreads in the lowest cohort into two buckets: performing assets and non-performing assets, which are defined as spreads above 1,000 bps.

The non-performing spread to worst is 2,818 bps, while the performing bucket — the biggest piece of the CCC market — is 461 bps, she said.

"It is isolated," she remarked. "I'm not necessarily sure that that will go away anytime soon, but it doesn't tell the story of overall concern and flashing caution for credit markets right now.".

For now, investors should remain selective within higher yield, Gerrity advised.

"We're looking for the best relative value opportunities, and we think that exists within that single-B cohort, and so we're leaning into that," she remarked.

Investors should be concerned if there is a steep widening in the broader high-yield market.

Sources indicate that but there's scant evidence of stress in the BB cohort. Spreads in that group are at 194 bps, up from 179 bps a year ago — although the move hasn't been in a straight line.

It has been revealed that "We're going to be focusing our attention on what are considered some stronger businesses," Martin said. "If we start to see the markets demand higher spreads there also, that's what we'll be looking at to see if risks are really rising.".

It's also important to understand that the Federal Reserve is raising rates in a strong economic environment, noted R.J. Gallo, chief investment officer of global fixed income at Federated Hermes. The central bank is concerned about an inflation problem amid high fossil fuel prices due to the Iran war, while growth has been stronger than expected, he noted.

"With growth being good as the reason that the Fed is hiking, then you wouldn't expect high yield to blow out because growth means revenues stay up, means cash flow and profitability stays up," he explained.

High yield becomes a disaster when the economy is heading into a sharp economic downturn, Gallo said.

"That's when spreads really widen out," he said. "But a recession is not the odds-on bet. Now, talk to me in six months if the Fed keeps hiking over and over, if oil prices stay high for longer, well, then maybe we will start to wonder.".

The aerospace and AI firm went public at $135 per share, closed at an all-time high of $201.80 four days later, but now trades at about $138 per share. Investors were initially impressed by its explosive growth, but its luster faded as rising interest rates and Treasury yields chilled the market.

Should investors buy SpaceX's stock as the bulls look the other way? Let's review two reasons to buy SpaceX -- as well as one reason to sell it -- to see if it's a contrarian investment.

NASDAQ · As of 4:00 PM ET 11/19/26.

In a recent development, starlink also acquired Grain Management's nationwide 800 MHz low-band spectrum, which previously belonged to T-Mobile (TMUS -0.91%), for $8 billion in October. That acquisition, which adds terrestrial cellular towers to its networks, could make it a formidable challenger to AT&T (T -0.46%), Verizon (T -0.46%), and other telco giants in the wireless carrier market.

According to recent reports, spaceX's Connectivity segment, which houses Starlink, is the company's only profitable business by generally accepted accounting principles (GAAP). Its ongoing growth should subsidize the expansion of its lower-margin space and SI ("super intelligence") businesses.

SpaceX has rolled out Starship, its largest rocket ever built, in 15 test flights since April 2023. It isn't a major revenue source for the Space segment yet, but it plans to launch 50-100 Starship rockets in 2027. That acceleration would likely widen its moat, dilute its expenses, and boost its adjusted earnings before interest, taxes, depreciation, and amortization (EBITDA) -- which remained negative in the first nine months of 2026 -- into positive territory.

Industry observers note that elon Musk believes the combined growth of Starlink, Starship, and its SI business will boost SpaceX's revenue from an estimated $49 billion this year to $1 trillion by 2030. With a market cap of $1.95 trillion, it trades at 40 times this year's sales but less than two times its 2030 target.

Reason to wait: SI's murky future.

Industry observers note that spaceX's Starlink and space segments have clear long-term catalysts, but the SI segment -- which houses X, xAI, Grok, Cursor, and its other AI assets -- faces a murkier future. The SI business generated $10.9 billion in revenue (40% of SpaceX's total revenue of $27.1 billion) in the first nine months of 2026, but it racked up an operating loss of $3.8 billion.

It has been revealed that that loss -- along with the Space segment's $1.2 billion operating loss -- nearly erased the Connectivity segment's operating profit of $5.21 billion. SpaceX still squeezed out a total operating profit of $705 million in the first nine months of the year, but that balancing act could falter as SpaceX ramps up its AI investments over the next few quarters.

Sources indicate that spaceX already plans to roughly double its capex sequentially, from $19.6 billion in the third quarter to $35-$40 billion in the fourth quarter, with most of that spending earmarked for Nvidia's (NVDA -3.30%) data center GPUs. That spending spree will continue to weigh down SpaceX's stock, especially if interest rates remain elevated.

In a recent development, with Anthropic's (ANT +17.07%) IPO sucking the oxygen out of the market and Nvidia dominating the headlines, it seems like fewer investors are paying attention to SpaceX. So if you can look past its near-term challenges and ride out the volatility, it might be a great time to accumulate the stock as it hovers near its IPO price. Over the long term, its three core growth engines -- space, Starlink, and SI -- could catapult its stock to fresh all-time highs.

  • Most of the major AIs offer a temporary chat or incognito option in which your conversation remains private and vanishes as soon as your chat ends.

  • Industry observers note that newly introduced to Google’s AI Mode is an option known as temporary threads.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Most of the major AIs offer a temporary chat or incognito option in which your conversation remains private and vanishes as soon as your chat ends. Now Google has jumped on board this bandwagon with its AI Mode searches.

Also: Google is making it easier to opt out of Gemini AI training.

Industry observers note that newly introduced to Google’s AI Mode is an option known as temporary threads. By choosing this setting, any searches you conduct in AI mode are detached from your own Google account and history. Your temporary searches won’t be affected by your past preferences or chats. They won’t be impacted by any personalization you’ve set up through your account. And they won’t be saved to your chat history. The goal here is to prevent anyone else, including Google, from accessing your conversations in this mode.

In a recent development, this option is presently rolling out around the world in all languages to Google search on both desktop and mobile browsers. You can run a temporary thread on any device and in any browser.

Try this for yourself: Head to the regular Google search page and click the button on the search field for AI Mode. You should then see an icon with a pen hovering over a dotted circle. If you don’t see it, you may have to run a search to get started. On the results page, you should then spot the icon.

Industry observers note that hover over the icon, and the tooltip will say: “Start temporary thread.” Click the icon on the left to start a upcoming thread. Now, any conversation you kick off will be temporary and unconnected to your account. But you don’t have to stick with just plain old text. Select the plus icon to upload an image or file. Select the microphone icon to speak instead of type.

Also: Goodbye, Gemini Gems: How to use Google’s latest Skills.

Sources indicate that certain limitations are in effect with a temporary thread. Specifically, you can’t do any of the following:.

Industry observers note that are these temporary threads truly private? Here’s what Google claims:.

Industry observers note that “Temporary threads will not be saved to your Google account and disappear after 24 hours,” Google remarked on a support page. “They won’t be used to train Google’s generative AI models, unless you submit feedback or it’s necessary for safety purposes. Google will still collect data and use data that is not associated with your account, including to keep our services working smoothly and safely and to support business operations.”.

It has been revealed that google also warns that your browser may still save your history if you visit a website within a temporary thread. Data could still be collected by the sites you visit and the services those sites use, including Google services like Google Analytics.

Also: I asked Gemini Notebook to ‘make me a site’ from my notes.

According to recent reports, for those reasons, you should still be cautious about the information you share even in a temporary thread. But certainly, this option provides greater privacy and protection than a regular AI Mode search.

It has been revealed that chatGPT, Gemini, and Microsoft Copilot all offer a temporary chat mode that also promises to keep your chats private and unconnected to your account. Claude and Perplexity provide the same feature but call it incognito mode.

I’m glad to see Google finally offering this option through its AI Mode searches. This marks the second privacy-friendly development in recent days from the search giant. On Tuesday, Google confirmed that it would be rolling out fresh settings through which you could opt out of AI model training without losing access to your chat history.

Industry News: What to Buy (and Skip) on Black Friday 2026
