⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Recent findings suggest that black Friday comes but once a year — although sometimes it feels like it lasts for a month.
  • If you’ve been sitting on a holiday shopping list and waiting for prices to drop, we’ve got good news: It’s time to start your shopping engines!
  • According to recent reports, you don’t need a calendar full of sale dates to navigate the shopping frenzy.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that black Friday comes but once a year — although sometimes it feels like it lasts for a month. The major day is Nov. 27, but the sales have already started.

If you’ve been sitting on a holiday shopping list and waiting for prices to drop, we’ve got good news: It’s time to start your shopping engines! (So to speak.).

According to recent reports, you don’t need a calendar full of sale dates to navigate the shopping frenzy. Focus on the categories likely to offer the biggest savings. Here’s what to buy, and what can wait.

If you’ve got top-priority toys on your list, buy them at a discount if you can find them, says Kristin McGrath, senior editor at The Krazy Coupon Lady, “just in case they don’t go down in price later.”.

Sources indicate that non-electronic toys are a good bet, says Julie Ramhold, consumer analyst with DealNews.com, because they’re less affected by tariffs on electronic components. That includes Legos, dolls and playsets.

Sources indicate that neeDoh squishies are a hot stocking stuffer this year and may be in short supply. At authorized retailers like Target, they should be relatively affordable, but try to avoid unauthorized resellers who may crank up the price, Ramhold notes.

While you may see mattress stores offering a few doorbusters on Black Friday, don’t feel pressured to jump on a deal.

Sources indicate that “Mattresses tend to see some of their strongest discounts around major sales events like Labor Day and Presidents Day,” says Ashley Feinstein Gerstley, shopping and savings strategist with Rakuten. “So if you’re not in a rush, it may be worth waiting for one of those windows.”.

Similarly, bedding and towels are often on deep discount during January white sales, Feinstein Gerstley notes.

Recent findings suggest that got some counter space and an itch for a new food processor? Black Friday sales are a great time to price surf for countertop appliances, including blenders, juicers and air fryers.

Industry observers note that “Those things we see sometimes half off or more,” McGrath states. “And they’re all on sale at the same time, so any one you’re looking for is likely to have a discount.”.

Holiday decor is only a must-buy during Black Friday sales if you need it for this holiday season.

While you’ll still see sales on holiday items like artificial trees, drinkware and garlands, “if you can wait until after Christmas, that’s when discounts should reach up to 80% or more at stores like Target, Walmart and department stores like JCPenney and Macy’s,” Ramhold says.

Sources indicate that electronics are typically a slam-dunk buy at this time of year. “Every store is competing for your business, so televisions, headphones, tablets, laptops — they’re all going to be on sale at the same time,” McGrath says.

Sources indicate that gaming consoles, in particular, see some of the better discounts. And they often come bundled with a gift card, gaming accessories or video games. “Consoles are common gifts,” McGrath states. “The stores know that, so they’re offering competitive deals.”.

That said, the traditional deep discounts you usually see on electronics for Black Friday may be a little lackluster this year due to high prices on parts, Ramhold says.

For best results, research the exact specs of the product you want and put it in your cart ahead of time, states consumer savings expert Andrea Woroch. That way, if a similar (but not identical) product goes on sale, you won’t accidentally buy the wrong thing.

You’ll usually find deeper discounts on items that are associated with fitness resolutions after New Year’s Day.

“Massive-box retailers like Target and department stores like Macy’s will offer up to 40% off or more on both fitness equipment and activewear during early January sales,” Ramhold says.

Sources indicate that many fashion retailers offer Black Friday sales, McGrath says. So if there’s an item you stock in multiple colors or a work staple you need to replace, keep an eye on your favorite sites for the markdowns.

Shoes, too, are a category to eyeball, including seasonal buys and everyday options like running shoes, Ramhold claims. “Some retailers may offer a BOGO promotion of some kind, but it’ll likely just be a ‘buy one, get one for 50% off,’” she says.

Just shop early for your size and color before inventory runs low, McGrath says. “You don’t want to miss out if there's a great deal.”.

According to recent reports, one caveat: Winter apparel will usually see bigger discounts toward the end of the year, Woroch says. So wait on your boot and coat purchases if you can.

Black Friday also offers the chance to snag deals on things you can use throughout the year:.

Photo gifts: Whether you’re ordering holiday cards or putting together a photo book for your in-laws (or yourself), you can usually find sales from vendors like Snapfish and Shutterfly, among others.

According to recent reports, fitness classes: Try your local gym, yoga or Pilates studio for discounts on class packs. “I’ll buy a 20-class package, and it’s always a great deal,” Woroch indicates.

Spa services: Check local businesses for deals on massages, manicures and other self-care treatments.

Streaming subscriptions: If you’re a upcoming customer (or canceled at least a month ago), some streaming platforms offer deep Black Friday discounts.

Black Friday deals are as much about strategy as savings, so make sure you’re maximizing your spending with these tips:.

Let AI help. Tools like ChatGPT and Gemini can do a lot of the legwork for you. Write out a product name and try prompts like “Find the lowest price for X product by comparing every retail site that it’s sold on and including coupons and cash back offers,” Woroch says. (Just note that AI searches can be limited and may not find every deal available.).

Recent findings suggest that check the price, not just the percentage: “Sometimes the base price is inflated or it was listed initially for a higher price,” Feinstein Gerstley notes. “Another retailer might have the same item for less, even if their discount doesn't look as impressive.”.

Use a browser extension or cash-back app. As long as you’re spending money, recapture some of it with a browser extension or cash-back app that sends a percentage of your purchase back to you.

Addas a preferred source on Google.

#50720. GTA 6 Launch Day Hits Different for Fired Rockstar Workers

📅 19 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 6m • 📚 Deep Dive (1110 w)

General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Cnet ↗ Open Full Page

GTA 6 Launch Day Hits Different for Fired Rockstar Workers

📅 19 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 6 min read (1110 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Cnet

⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • As people across the world sneak a day away from the office to play the long-awaited Grand Theft Auto 6 on Thursday, the Rockstar employees who made the game are hopefully enjoying a well-earned day off in celebration.
  • For the 34 workers based in the UK and Canada who Rockstar dismissed in October 2025, GTA 6 launch day isn’t the day of celebration it should’ve been.
  • Sources indicate that “I should be with my team, taking a photo at every poster I can see, and be happy about it,” indicates Branimira Yordanova, who worked for three years in the lighting department at Rockstar North in Edinburgh, Scotland.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

As people across the world sneak a day away from the office to play the long-awaited Grand Theft Auto 6 on Thursday, the Rockstar employees who made the game are hopefully enjoying a well-earned day off in celebration. But not everyone who worked on the cultural juggernaut is joining the victory lap.

For the 34 workers based in the UK and Canada who Rockstar dismissed in October 2025, GTA 6 launch day isn’t the day of celebration it should’ve been.

Sources indicate that “I should be with my team, taking a photo at every poster I can see, and be happy about it,” indicates Branimira Yordanova, who worked for three years in the lighting department at Rockstar North in Edinburgh, Scotland. “But it’s impossible because of how much hurt the firing has caused everyone.”.

Rockstar fired the workers on the spot — something that’s only legal in the UK in cases of gross misconduct — alleging that they’d shared confidential company information on a Discord server.

According to recent reports, the workers tell a different story. They say the company had long been aware of the Discord server, and only fired them when it started to look as though their efforts to unionize might succeed. They believe they were made an example of.

On the evening before the game’s launch, I spoke with Yordanova and her former colleague Dayne Oram, a senior production coordinator who had been at Rockstar North for seven years and was also affected by the dismissals, about how they were feeling about launch day.

According to recent reports, “One of our fellow colleagues mentioned it the best,” claims Yordanova. “What we’ll feel tomorrow is mourning what could have been, whether we want to or not.”.

Recent findings suggest that for all those who are mourning, others among the fired workers still hold a candle for GTA. Jacob Jones, who spent one year as a game tester before taking a role as a designer on the open world team for four years, was raring to play the game on launch day.

In a recent development, jones graduated from being a childhood fan of the franchise – even counting the signatures of Rockstar co-founders Sam and Dan Hauser among his merch collection – to his dream job. He remains a GTA fan to this day, but describes feeling a sense of “poignance” and “bittersweetness” toward the launch.

For Oram, Yordanova and Jones, GTA 6 eve was already a heavy day, even aside from the launch fever.

According to recent reports, they’re all part of a case brought by the Independent Workers’ Union of Great Britain on behalf of 23 former Rockstar North employees, who say they were unfairly dismissed for union activity. Hours before Oram and Yordanova spoke with me, a Glasgow employment tribunal had heard Rockstar’s closing submissions, which now leaves the fired workers in limbo as they wait for a verdict.

According to recent reports, rockstar North maintains that it fired the employees for gross misconduct. The organization didn’t respond to a request for further comment.

Oram, Yordanova and Jones all speak highly of their former colleagues and teams, but Oram calls the sacking a “traumatic experience.” None have managed to secure alternative employment in the past 13 months. Jones notes for now he’s focused on getting justice.

Sources indicate that meanwhile, reminders of their former employer have been everywhere as the studio geared up to release perhaps the most highly anticipated game of all time. Billboards, buses and online ads have been impossible to avoid, leaving Yordanova feeling “devastated.”.

Recent findings suggest that “I’ve genuinely had to make sure to avoid looking at it,” she says. “It’s such a cool game, and to know that you worked on it, you feel a sense of pride and joy to see it out. But it’s like that sense of joy has been taken away from us in such a ruthless manner.”.

Oram acknowledges having “mixed feelings” about the launch. It’s been fantastic watching video footage of people playing and reviewing the game, they say. At the same time, they’ve found it difficult not being able to celebrate the moment with their former team.

In a recent development, the workers fired from Rockstar North had varying ideas about whether they wanted to celebrate the launch, or avoid it entirely. Jones is one of those who started playing the game as soon as he got home from the tribunal at 1 a.m. By the time we spoke on Thursday, he’d played around six or seven hours.

In a recent development, “I personally think it’s a masterpiece,” he indicates. Even though he worked on the game, he’s discovering surprises everywhere. “I haven’t completed it yet, but I do think it is probably the greatest game ever made.”.

Recent findings suggest that oram notes that they planned to stick with watching streams of the game on launch day. “I’m probably not going to play the game for a little while, but I am looking forward to at least watching some people,” they say. Oram worked across so many bits of the game that there’s plenty they’re excited to see people discover.

Yordanova says she’s firmly in the avoidance camp. “I was really excited about playing the game in its official form because obviously when you work on it, you get to play it,” she says. “Even while we were in the office, there were parts I was really excited about – but I don’t think I’ll be playing it for the foreseeable future.”.

It has been revealed that she hopes that one day her feelings will change, she adds. “But right now, that’s just not possible in any way.”.

Instead, she’ll be spending the day with friends who supported her over the last year. She plans to “dive into another art form” by seeing the stop-motion animated film Wildwood at the cinema, which particularly appeals to her as a lighting artist.

According to recent reports, many people playing GTA 6 around the world won’t be aware of what happened to Oram, Yordanova, Jones and their colleagues during the game’s development, but the affected workers would like people to know. “I understand people just want to focus on the joy, but I don’t think you can separate the launch with what happened,” says Yordanova.

Recent findings suggest that reflecting on what happened, Jones claims it’s such a shame the way things went down. “It was my absolute passion,” he says. “I just wish that the circumstances were different, and I would have loved to have still been there working on games. I wish I got to the end.”.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • From the kernel all the way up to the desktop environment, you get to determine what is used and even how it is used.
  • Also: My favorite Linux desktop environment for laptops surprised even me.
  • If there’s one thing that separates Linux from all other operating systems, it’s the willingness to try something different.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Linux is all about choice. From the kernel all the way up to the desktop environment, you get to determine what is used and even how it is used. The staggering number of distributions, desktops, package managers, file managers, and terminal apps provide you with a nearly infinite combination of choices. That choice is and has always been a key aspect of Linux.

Also: My favorite Linux desktop environment for laptops surprised even me.

So too is innovation. If there’s one thing that separates Linux from all other operating systems, it’s the willingness to try something different. Linux developers are always pushing the limits of what an operating system is, and this fresh take on the OS is the epitome of that.

The distribution in question is called Pond. According to the developers, “Pond is an opportunity for us to play with familiar conventions and experiment with new ideas that make a computer more natural and satisfying.”.

It has been revealed that the developers have achieved something special. Pond takes the standard UI and turns it on its head. Part tiling window manager, part mobile UI, part GNOME, and part something we’ve never before seen, this desktop environment is special. It took me all of five minutes to fall in love with what they’ve created.

The Pond UI consists of the following:.

Also: The only 4 Linux email clients I recommend.

If you’ve ever considered using a tiling window manager, but thought the lack of a mouse made it seem a bit too complicated, Pond is exactly what you want. Here’s how it works:.

Sources indicate that pond uses the Niri window manager to arrange windows in columns along an infinite strip from left to right. In multi-monitor setups, each display gets its own strip, so windows never “overflow” from one monitor to the next.

Also: How to install Arch Linux without losing your mind.

It has been revealed that at the same time, workspaces are dynamic, and there’s always a newly introduced workspace automatically created to the right of the farthest-right window. The combination of the Pond sidebar and Niri’s way of handling windows makes this UI truly original.

In a recent development, pond doesn’t have a traditional desktop menu. Instead, you open the launcher (using the Super+Space key combination), type the name of the app you want to install, and hit Enter when the app name appears on both the display and as an icon in the top portion of the sidebar.

Another thing that sets Pond apart is how you install apps. Yes, you can open a terminal window and install an app using the pacman command, or you can open the launcher, type install, press Enter, and then type the name of the app you want to install. For instance, if you wanted to install LibreOffice, you would type:.

According to recent reports, once you hit Enter a second time, the installation will begin. Many apps install via Flatpak, but on the off-chance an app must be installed via the pacman package manager, you’ll be prompted to type your user password before the installation begins.

As I hinted earlier, Pond is based on Arch Linux, which means it’s a rolling-release distribution. One matter that did give me pause was the lack of a GUI update system, which indicates that updates would have to happen in the terminal, like so:.

It has been revealed that I installed the Shelly GUI frontend, which does have an patch component. Personally, I would simply open the terminal window, type sudo pacman -Syu, hit Enter, and let the update run in the background. But if a GUI is your jam, Shelly is what you want.

Also: A super fast distro for anyone ready to move beyond beginner Linux.

It would be sweet if the developers allowed updating the system from within the launcher, so it didn’t require opening the terminal first. The Pond launcher does allow running system commands from the launcher, which will then open the terminal window and execute the command. For instance, open the terminal, type a command, hit Enter, and then scroll through the list of available commands that can be run.

Pond ships with kernel 7.3.4-3, so it has outstanding hardware recognition and performance.

Recent findings suggest that you should definitely give Pond a try, especially if you’re adventurous and want to experience something completely different. If, on the other hand, different is not in your stream, then Pond will frustrate you to no end.

Also: Why Nextcloud Office is my new favorite free productivity suite.

According to recent reports, pond excited me more than any OS has in a very long time; so much so that I could see this becoming my go-to OS, once it reaches stable release. Until then, I will keep Pond installed on a laptop, keep upgrading, and see what happens next.

Kudos to the Pond OS team for coming up with something truly unique in an already competitive world.

💡 Key Takeaways

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By RJ Fulton – Nov 19, 2026 at 4:50PM EST.

Wall Street's sell-off intensified on Thursday, November 19, as selling pressure spread across nearly every sector of the market. The Dow Jones Industrial Average (^DJI -2.19%) plunged more than 1,100 points, falling 2.19% to 49,097 and moving closer to correction territory. Meanwhile, the S&P 500 (^GSPC -2.02%) fell 2.00% to 7,177, marking its sixth consecutive session of losses, while the Nasdaq Composite (^IXIC -2.25%) dropped 2.23% to 23,886 as investors continued to retreat from growth stocks.

According to recent reports, selling pressure extended beyond equities, with gold falling 2.10% to $3,663.50. The 10-year Treasury yield eased three basis points to 5.07%, offering little relief to equity markets. Energy and consumer staples were among the few sectors to finish in positive territory, gaining 0.14% and 0.04%, respectively, while industrials plunged 2.61%.

Despite the broader market sell-off, Insmed (INSM +20.58%) surged 20.58% following reports that French pharmaceutical giant Sanofi (SNY -2.25%) is considering an acquisition of the biotechnology firm. Palo Alto Networks (PANW +6.42%) also bucked the broader trend, gaining 6.42% after reporting stronger-than-expected quarterly earnings and announcing a $4.5 billion acquisition.

It has been revealed that conversely, Advanced Micro Devices (AMD -7.72%) plunged 7.72% following a media report alleging ties to a blacklisted Chinese server manufacturer. The report adds another layer of regulatory uncertainty to a semiconductor industry already grappling with tightening U.S. export restrictions and deteriorating investor sentiment.

Perhaps the most concerning development on Wall Street is how broadly selling pressure has spread. What initially appeared to be a pullback driven by elevated technology valuations is increasingly developing into a broader market downturn. Meta Muse booked an Airbnb without permission – and that’s not the worst of it

💡 Key Takeaways
  • It has been revealed that meta’s Muse AI agent has only been around for a few months, but already has a track record of user privacy violations.
  • Meta’s AI agent can still access your private messages.
  • According to a Reuters investigation, Meta employees testing Muse mentioned the agent messaged them about topics they hadn’t asked it about, including career advice, a follow-up on a request for childcare, products they hadn’t purchased, and, crucially, bank account balances they didn’t recognize.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that meta’s Muse AI agent has only been around for a few months, but already has a track record of user privacy violations. Even Meta employees are reporting concerning incidents, including the agent taking actions they didn’t ask it to and sharing information they didn’t recognize that appears to belong to other users.

Also: Don’t use Muse? Meta’s AI agent can still access your private messages.

According to a Reuters investigation, Meta employees testing Muse mentioned the agent messaged them about topics they hadn’t asked it about, including career advice, a follow-up on a request for childcare, products they hadn’t purchased, and, crucially, bank account balances they didn’t recognize.

These incidents “prompted unnerved employees to raise concerns it could be mixing up conversations between different accounts and exposing users’ private data,” Reuters said.

Reuters remarked “an employee told colleagues his Muse had randomly added an extra message to its regular chats about fishing-related weather and tide information, saying: ‘BTW, two bank updates, your Capital One balance is $2,722.58, your Charles Schwab balance is $5,899.57.'” In another instance, Muse booked a non-refundable Airbnb for an employee who hadn’t instructed it to.

Muse notified another employee, who was using the agent on her personal phone, about a message she’d received on Signal, though she said she hadn’t given the agent access to the encrypted messaging app.

Also: Meta Muse is the worst AI agent for privacy – and I’ve tried them all.

Reuters and the AI Now Institute determined, through testing on an Android phone and a Mac, that Muse used “permissions granted during the bot’s initial setup to pull in the message text, leveraging those authorizations in ways a user might not anticipate.” Because Muse is set up with automatic access to Android push notifications, it didn’t need explicit app access to read messages.

The tests did not work on an iPhone, suggesting better protections against Muse’s prying.

It has been revealed that similarly, in September, a user reported Muse had shared his address with a Facebook Marketplace buyer before checking with him. The incident was ultimately a misunderstanding between the terms the user thought he’d consented to and how much access he was actually handing over, which exemplifies that Meta and the user may have explicitly different definitions of access, and that Muse can take advantage of that grey area.

Meta told Reuters these incidents were either isolated or the result of hallucinations, though Reuters could not confirm that.

These are just the latest in a string of alarming incidents surrounding Muse. In its first month, a cybersecurity professional discovered Muse had a serious zero-day bug that made it hijackable. At least one journalist found the AI sifting through his Apple Messages after he’d explicitly denied those permissions, which Apple then issued stronger privacy protections to address. Banks have also blocked agents over concerns.

Recent findings suggest that as a company, Meta doesn’t have a solid history of respecting user privacy. That legacy is partly what informed ZDNET contributor David Gewirtz’s suspicion of the AI assistant when he tested it, though it earned his assigned title of “worst AI agent for privacy” all on its own. The agent asked him for everything from contacts and chats to his logins and passwords, and Meta automatically uses conversations with Muse to train its AI.

Also: How I safely run my OpenClaw AI agent 24/7 on a Mac.

Recent findings suggest that public awareness of the risks of AI agents hit a peak last year with the viral OpenClaw. The predominant advice for using agents has been to take every privacy precaution: Be careful with the data you share and the apps you give it permissions for, and watch what you tell it. But if users believe they’re doing so by restricting access to certain apps, just for Muse to find a way in anyway, privacy hygiene isn’t enough.

Also: How to keep your chatbot conversations as private as possible.

Reuters’ findings may provide an opportunity for Google’s agentic offering, now called Tasks (formerly Spark), which it made free (with usage limits, like Muse) this week.

Holiday sales like Black Friday and Cyber Monday usually have good personal tech deals on TVs, wearables and robot vacuums. It’s also a good time to shop for a fresh laptop, but not every brand is worth your time and money.

According to recent reports, we recently surveyed CNET readers as part of our People’s Picks awards to get their opinion on their laptop brand — including their take on its battery life, durability and performance for gaming and graphics. Our readers could choose from many popular laptop brands, but one was a clear favorite. It claimed eight awards, including the overall winner for CNET’s People’s Pick award. And it’s the one worth heavily considering if you plan to buy a latest laptop while there are holiday savings.

Industry observers note that apple wins the overall award in CNET’s People’s Picks, and also takes home the overall satisfaction rating, with 74.2% of Apple users saying they’re extremely satisfied with their laptop. In comparison, 22.5% say they’re satisfied — bringing Apple to a near-perfect overall satisfaction score of 96.7%.

Apple’s overall impression also speaks to other awards it wins from CNET readers, including high ratings for its impressive battery life, display quality and high-quality build. All of those categories and more sum up Apple’s brand loyalty nod, with 68% of MacBook owners saying they would buy the same laptop and model from Apple again.

In a recent development, how much are people paying for MacBooks? CNET found that 43.5% of Apple users paid at least $1,500. Until earlier in 2026, the MacBook Air was Apple’s entry-level laptop, priced at least $1,299. The introduction of the budget-friendly MacBook Neo brought that down to a more reasonable $699. However, despite Apple’s laptops being more expensive than those from other brands, they still ranked high for their value proposition. Part of the reason for that is that MacBooks received high marks for hardware reliability. “Apple’s MacBooks might cost more than the average laptop, but their premium build quality means they’re built for the long haul,” said Matt Elliott, CNET’s laptop editor.

It has been revealed that if you plan to have your laptop for a while, you may be impressed by other features that make work easier and faster, like its M-series central processing unit for task management and AI capabilities, great battery life and a one-of-a-kind operating system — right now MacOS 27. All of the features and specifications bundled together make Apple’s perception as a high-end laptop worth the investment for long-term satisfaction.

It has been revealed that apple clinches a near-perfect score for its value perception. According to our survey results, 44% of Apple users noted their MacBook has exceptional value. Others say their MacBook is worth what they paid for it (50.9%) — for a total positive score of 94.6%.

In a recent development, digging deeper into Apple’s cost-to-value rating, 81.8% of Apple owners paid at least $1,000 for their laptops, which may seem costly, but Apple users seem OK with the price. That could be because, even though Apple has only three laptop models in a handful of sizes in its lineup, each one delivers solid performance and storage.

Recent findings suggest that take Apple’s proprietary processing chips, for example — each upgrade since the M1 release has improved the laptop’s speed, battery life and performance. Now the M6 can handle the MacBook’s AI capabilities, storage and high-resolution graphics. And for all of that power, most MacBooks are relatively thin and lightweight, making them easier for mobility — just a few of the reasons Apple owners may be OK with paying more for what they’re getting.

According to recent reports, battery life is a significant deal for many laptop buyers, and that’s another area where Apple delivers. Over a quarter of those surveyed (25.7%) noted their MacBook’s battery life exceeds 10 hours — which is more than enough for a full day of work in most cases. And 18.7% say their MacBook’s battery lasts between 8 and 10 hours — totaling 44.4% of MacBook users saying their battery lasts 8 hours or more.

According to recent reports, comparatively, non-Apple laptop brands fall short in this category. Only 16.4% of Lenovo people say their laptop’s battery lasts at least 8 hours, and even fewer for Dell (12.7%) and HP (11.8%). If you’re leaning toward a MacBook for its battery life, CNET’s lab test shows that the MacBook Neo lasts 13 hours and 26 minutes for online streaming, whereas the Apple MacBook Air 13-inch M5 (2026 model) lasts 17 hours and 2 minutes.

Apple sweeps the brightness, color accuracy and clarity category with 99.2% of its consumers either satisfied or extremely satisfied with their laptop’s screen performance. No Apple users reported dissatisfaction.

“Apple has long been a favorite for creative professionals and content creators for good reason: Its MacBook displays are some of the best you’ll find on any laptop,” said Josh Goldman, CNET’s managing editor for computers. “While Apple may use marketing names like Retina and Liquid Retina to describe display features, they do translate into sharp and clear text and images, with excellent brightness, contrast, color gamut coverage and color accuracy.”.

According to recent reports, the new MacBook Pro with PROLED XDR even goes beyond what MacBook users have come to expect. It’s Apple’s first OLED touchscreen laptop and features next-level brightness, color and contrast.

Apple receives high ratings: 80% of MacBook owners say it has premium build quality, 18.2% say it’s solid, and those results don’t surprise us.

Recent findings suggest that and MacBooks seem durable and reliable, with 87% of Apple consumers reporting no hardware failures on their MacBooks, while 8% say minor software fixes resolved their issues. Only 3% needed minor hardware repairs, and 2.2% needed major repairs — which could be fixes such as a battery or screen replacement.

It has been revealed that our editors say the M5 MacBook Air is thin and lightweight, but still has a well-built aluminum design. And the M5 Pro MacBook Pro is sturdy, too. What sets Apple’s laptop hardware apart could be its aluminum chassis — the casing that holds all of the components together.

“Apple makes three lines of MacBooks — the Neo, Air and Pro — and focuses on making those the best they can possibly be. They are all built to deliver a premium experience using high-quality materials, and that even includes the entry-level MacBook Neo,” said Goldman.

Lastly, Apple uses durable materials, such as the 100% recycled aluminum alloy it states encloses the 14-inch MacBook Pro. And the tech giant has several testing facilities to test MacBook durability.

Sources indicate that when it comes to getting your daily tasks done, most CNET readers with MacBooks (70.9%) say Apple’s laptops handle workloads flawlessly. It’s worth noting that 45% use their MacBook for work tasks, but no Apple users reported poor performance.

According to recent reports, here’s why that might be: Apple’s laptops are packed with top-notch performance specs and features, like their powerful processors, unified memory and fast storage. Better processor performance means enhanced graphics, on-device AI capabilities and faster task speeds, all of which add up to being able to finish work, play games or stream videos without challenges or lags caused by your laptop’s hardware.

It has been revealed that on the software side, MacOS 27 Golden Gate gives you built-in AI features, like Siri AI and Visual Intelligence. And you can organize your Safari tabs by topic and use the Notify Me tool to be notified of website changes, like price drops or breaking news. Plus, you can create shortcuts to automate tasks. Coupling all of these features and specifications explains why Apple users rate MacBooks so highly for getting the job done.

Apple leads the way on brand retention with 68% of Apple consumers planning to buy the same MacBook model again, while 29.1% would buy another model from Apple’s lineup. Only 3% would switch to another brand that’s not Apple.

Usually, when you buy one Apple product, you’re likely to stick to the brand’s ecosystem, especially since Apple has its own operating systems to access its unique features and work seamlessly with other Apple products with Apple’s Continuity feature. For example, you can start an email on your iPhone, but finish typing it on your MacBook. Or you can call or send a text from your laptop without reaching for your iPhone. Other features work across Apple devices, including iCloud, Universal Clipboard and AirDrop.

Industry observers note that asus wins as a midtier laptop choice with 67% of Asus owners paying between $500 and $1,499. There’s a sweet spot in this range with 38% spending between $500 and $999, and 28% paying between $1,000 and $1,499.

If you’re planning to spend that amount on a newly introduced laptop, you may also be pleased to know that Asus earns a higher satisfaction rating compared with other non-Apple laptop brands — 48% of Asus people say they’re extremely satisfied.

Sources indicate that asus laptops have a few features and specifications that may speak to that rating, regardless of budget. Asus has other laptops worth exploring depending on your needs, like the budget-friendly Asus ZenBook S 14 or the premium Asus ROG Zephyrus G14 that could be good for gamers and creators.

Recent findings suggest that over one-third of Acer laptop owners (38%) paid less than $500 for their laptop — which is greater than other laptop brands in this price range. If you’re impressed by Acer’s value and satisfaction scores, there are a few budget-friendly Acer options to consider. The Acer Aspire 16 AI wins CNET’s Editors’ Choice award. According to recent reports, even though Apple is highly recommended by CNET readers, there are plenty of other laptop models and brands worth considering depending on your needs. Goldman said Lenovo has such a large and varied PC selection using the latest chips from Intel, AMD, Qualcomm and Nvidia that there is something for everyone and every budget. Even those who spend less on a Lenovo laptop can expect solid performance, including battery life.

If your laptop’s hardware fails or it breaks, you may be in the market for a newly introduced laptop sooner than expected. Think about cooling fan problems, overheating or your laptop not powering on at all. Over half (68%) of Lenovo laptop owners mentioned they haven’t had any hardware issues with their laptops — the most compared to other non-MacBooks.

In a recent development, beyond hardware durability, Lenovo also scores highly for its build and construction — overall making it a sturdy laptop choice. In our survey, 38% of Lenovo laptop owners say their laptop has a premium feel, while 51% say it’s solid — totaling a positive score of 89%.

If you’re looking for recommendations, the Lenovo Yoga Slim 7x Gen 11 has an all-metal design. Asus wins over nearly half of its laptop owners, with 47.5% giving it an exceptional value rating  — exceeding expectations for its price. Take our Editors’ Choice pick, the Asus Zenbook A14. It has been revealed that asus is the top non-Apple laptop option to consider for tasks, with 47.7% of CNET readers giving it high ratings. Recent findings suggest that asus scores highest for its screen brightness and clarity, with over half (51%) extremely satisfied with its screen quality and brightness, while 38.6% say they’re satisfied, giving Asus an overall satisfaction rate of 90%. 📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

If you're here looking for lower mortgage interest rates, today is definitely not your day.

According to recent reports, the average interest rate on a 30-year, fixed-rate mortgage jumped to 7.38% APR, according to rates provided to NerdWallet by Zillow. This is 25 basis points higher than yesterday and 12 basis points higher than a week ago. (A basis point is one one-hundredth of a percentage point.).

In a recent development, keep in mind that mortgage rates are always on the move, and that if you're tracking rates day-to-day, you're going to see a lot of volatility. Zooming out and looking at the bigger picture — like a graph showing at least a month's worth of rate data — can help you see the overall trend.

Here are the average APRs we're seeing today, as well as movement over the past month for context:.

» Take the next step: Compare mortgage rates from NerdWallet’s top lenders.

In a recent development, mortgage rates are constantly changing, since a major part of how rates are set depends on reactions to fresh inflation reports, job numbers, Fed meetings, global news ... you name it. For example, even tiny changes in the bond market can shift mortgage pricing.

Industry observers note that on Friday, the Bureau of Labor Statistics released the Producer Price Index for October, which tracks the change in prices that U.S. producers are able to get for their products. This is one way to measure inflation on the market end, rather than the consumer end.

The results were mixed. While prices didn’t rise quite as high as economists anticipated month-over-month (0.3% vs. 0.4%), year-over-year price growth did reach 6.5% — the largest increase in four years. This points to even higher costs for consumers coming in the near future.

Investors are convinced that the Federal Reserve will raise overnight borrowing rates again in December to pull inflation down. And higher overnight borrowing rates — called the federal funds rate, which is what banks pay to fund products like mortgages — usually lead to higher mortgage rates.

» MORE: How the Federal Reserve affects mortgage rates.

Refinancing might make sense if today’s rates are at least 0.5 to 0.75 of a percentage point lower than your current rate (and if you strategy to stay in your home long enough to break even on closing costs).

With rates where they are right now, you may want to start considering a refi if your current rate is around 7.88% or higher — but there aren’t many people for whom that’s true.

Also consider your goals: Are you trying to lower your monthly payment, shorten your loan term or turn home equity into cash? For example, you might be more comfortable with paying a higher rate for a cash-out refinance than you would for a rate-and-term refinance, so long as the overall costs are lower than if you kept your original mortgage and added a HELOC or home equity loan.

If you're looking for a lower rate, use NerdWallet's refinance calculator to estimate savings and understand how long it would take to break even on the costs of refinancing.

Industry observers note that » Time to refi? Compare refinance rates from NerdWallet’s top lenders.

There is no universal “right” time to start shopping — what matters is whether you can comfortably afford a mortgage now at today’s rates.

In a recent development, if the answer is yes, don’t get too hung up on whether you could be missing out on lower rates later; you can refinance down the road. Focus on getting preapproved, comparing lender offers, and understanding what monthly payment works for your budget.

NerdWallet’s affordability calculator can help you estimate your potential monthly payment. If a latest home isn’t in the cards right now, there are still things you can do to strengthen your buyer profile. Take this time to pay down existing debts and build your down payment savings. Not only will this free up more cash flow for a future mortgage payment, it can also get you a better interest rate when you’re ready to buy.

Apple’s Support Community Shuts Down Tomorrow, Removing User Discussions

📅 19 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (919 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Cnet

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • According to recent reports, on Friday, Apple’s Support Communities website will shut down permanently, removing decades of Apple owner conversations.
  • A notification on the community forum appeared last Tuesday, warning visitors that the site was shutting and would be offline entirely on Nov.
  • Apple was a pioneer in community support forums before the aughts, letting people discuss their Mac complications as early as 1998.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, on Friday, Apple’s Support Communities website will shut down permanently, removing decades of Apple owner conversations. For a few hours more, the website will still be read-only, but I’ve found the search function intermittently crashes, so even that ability isn’t very reliable.

A notification on the community forum appeared last Tuesday, warning visitors that the site was shutting and would be offline entirely on Nov. 20. If you want to look up a specific Apple troubleshooting topic on iPhones or HomePods, you should do it this evening. Soon, the entire peer advice and support site, which has been operating for nearly three decades, will be gone.

Apple was a pioneer in community support forums before the aughts, letting people discuss their Mac complications as early as 1998. For those of you who might remember, that’s the year Apple debuted its iMac G3, the desktop with a translucent blue teardrop-shaped case. The iMac G3 abandoned legacy ports and the floppy disk drive in favor of CD-ROM and USB.

Back then, the site was called Apple Tech Exchange, later renamed Apple Discussions until it eventually became the Apple Support Community in 2011. Many still turned to forums for DIY solutions, using it to get advice from other tinkerers interested in figuring out how to fix things on their own.

According to recent reports, an Apple spokesperson told CNET the decision was made “after careful evaluation of our strategy and our customers’ needs.” Apple’s site notification directs people to visit the official Apple Support site. You’ll also be able to use Apple’s online chat, support phone numbers and in-store support, the same way they worked in the past.

In a recent development, apple is one of the first American tech companies to give up its community discussion site — Google still has Google Communities Help, and Amazon manages its own forum domain with discussions from both staff and users. But Apple’s sudden closure could indicate a major shift, with others eventually following suit. It has highlighted an ongoing discussion about the role of peer support in tech, how AI has changed our online conversations and more.

When news of the shutdown spread, Apple users flocked to the internet to express everything from dismay to vindication.

For many, the Apple Support Community forums were controversial, not least because it wasn’t always clear how they worked. The site contained “user-submitted content, comments and opinions” and was “for informational purposes only,” yet many would mistake it for official Apple Support from staff.

According to recent reports, in discussions on Reddit about the closure, many bemoaned the absence of real Apple employees from the site’s forums and found the advice from other Support Community consumers to often be frustrating and not worth the effort. On the unofficial Apple subreddit, many mourned the loss of community while also noting that answers on the forum were often much harder to come by. Others said the site grew less helpful over the years.

It has been revealed that CNET phone reviewer and senior editor Mike Sorrentino told me that the forum shutdown “will likely drive customers looking for help with basic questions to Apple’s official support articles rather than user-created threads.” But Sorrentino also acknowledged that the move reflects a general trend away from the site, with more people getting answers from sites like Reddit. “Apple’s always been big on controlling what information is shown on its website, and in that view, moving away from user discussion makes sense,” he said.

Sources indicate that just this week, I used the Apple Support Community site when looking for an answer to a problem implementing Apple Intelligence on my home security cameras, which required jumping through multiple hoops. Perhaps tellingly, I ended up finding the correct answer on Reddit myself. But that could become harder to do in the near future.

The shutdown of Apple’s peer support forums is definitely a sign of the times, especially as tech companies push customers away from repairing their own devices and toward replacing them outright — or at least encourage device owners to pay for official support services. It’s also a sign of the growing role of artificial intelligence, which is capitalizing on user-created content to provide summaries, moving people away from organic discussion and exchange on sites like these.

Reddit has lucrative data-licensing contracts with Google and OpenAI, allowing the companies to train their AI models on Reddit’s massive archive of human discussions, as well as surface Reddit content in tools like Google AI Overviews and ChatGPT. Reddit is also moving to a login-only viewing mode, making it significantly harder for casual users to find answers unless they trust AI summaries.

In a recent development, apple may be leery of keeping so much user knowledge online for AI models to scrape for their own answers. The manufacturer may also want to prevent AI summaries from providing information from past forum consumers on how to jailbreak Apple devices or DIY fixes, even as the EU has mandated that Apple start building replaceable batteries by next year. And it wouldn’t be a good look if Siri AI started regurgitating incorrect or outdated info it had picked up from Apple’s own sites.

According to recent reports, whatever the reason, the circle of Apple people helping users has grown smaller, and that doesn’t bode well for support forums as a whole. It may be time to start archiving those years of data before other tech companies implement similar aims.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • A Redditor recently shared that they were struggling to decide which financial steps to take first after a job loss.
  • Should they withdraw money from retirement savings to have more cash on hand — but pay an early withdrawal penalty?
  • Many users responded with good ideas: File for unemployment, try to avoid tapping into retirement savings, and cut expenses as much as possible.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

A Redditor recently shared that they were struggling to decide which financial steps to take first after a job loss.

Should they withdraw money from retirement savings to have more cash on hand — but pay an early withdrawal penalty? Or is it better to rely on the severance payout to handle expenses?

Many users responded with good ideas: File for unemployment, try to avoid tapping into retirement savings, and cut expenses as much as possible.

For more ideas, I asked three financial experts how to manage money in the immediate aftermath of job loss.

While it’s tempting to make quick decisions about tapping into a retirement fund or selling a house, it’s better to wait on any massive moves, says Parker Wine, retirement planning advisor at the financial firm Daniel A. White & Associates in Lewes, Delaware.

That’s because you need time to digest the situation and weigh the pros and cons of different options, he says. “People can get impulsive and panic, and it’s usually a bad thing to make decisions when you’re panicking,” he says.

Take your time, get second opinions and think through all of your options first, Wine suggests.

If you’re fortunate enough to receive a severance package, wait to sign it until you’ve reviewed it carefully and understand all of the details, notes John Rafferty, partner and investment advisor representative at Solomon Financial in Carmel, Indiana.

For example, make sure you know about your health insurance options, such as whether you’ll receive insurance through COBRA or need to take out a latest policy in the health insurance marketplace.

Filing for unemployment and checking into any other available workplace benefits — such as help with your new job search — is also an crucial part of understanding what support to expect in the weeks and months ahead, Rafferty adds.

Creating a bare-bones budget stripped of “extras” like restaurant meals or travel can help the severance payment last as long as possible, Rafferty says.

“Now that you don’t have income coming in, ask yourself, ‘How much can I spend and where?’”.

You might be able to cut back on entertainment costs, coffee runs and clothing purchases, for example.

At the same time, it’s key to prioritize the essentials like mortgage payments, rent, utilities and food. Rafferty recommends calling your mortgage organization, utilities provider and any other lenders to ask if they have a hardship program for those experiencing financial challenges.

Opting in could give you more time to pay your bills or temporarily lower payments.

It’s hard to stick to a budget that eliminates all entertainment, so Rafferty suggests finding enjoyable activities that come with a low price tag. Hiking, discovering a new park and participating in free community events are all ways to enjoy downtime on a budget.

In a recent development, “Having that release is mentally a big thing so you can stay prepared for the job search,” he claims. “Otherwise, it’s easy to get down and feel negative, and we need things to help us feel positive.”.

Similarly, connecting with friends and family during this time is crucial, indicates Laura Adams, accredited financial counselor and financial coach in Wilmington, North Carolina.

Recent findings suggest that people often feel a sense of shame or embarrassment after job loss, and Adams encourages people to talk about their feelings and ask for help if needed. “Financial shame can cause us to make emotional rather than confident financial decisions,” she indicates.

Recent findings suggest that starting some kind of side hustle to bring in extra cash can also help bridge the gap between the job loss and your next job, Wine says. Substitute teaching, working at a local public golf course and driving for a rideshare service are all options he’s seen people try.

Doing something upcoming also helps stave off boredom while unemployed, but he cautions that you’ll still owe taxes on any side income you bring in, so plan accordingly.

Sources indicate that all three financial experts also emphasized that a job loss is easier to handle with an emergency savings fund you can turn to, and suggested building one up — ideally three to six months’ worth of expenses. But starting small helps, too — while employed, if possible.

The Redditor who posted the question mentioned that, like many Americans, they lacked emergency savings. This added urgency to the question of what to prioritize.

Reddit is an online forum where users share their thoughts in “threads” on various topics. The popular site includes plenty of discussion on financial subjects like how to deal with job loss, so we sifted through Reddit forums to get a pulse check. People post anonymously, so we cannot confirm their individual experiences or circumstances.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • 10 stocks we like better than Peloton Interactive ›.
  • According to recent reports, peloton Interactive (PTON -5.23%) stock peaked at around $163 in late 2020, which was a whopping 462% increase from its initial public offering (IPO) price of $29.
  • According to recent reports, but as lockdowns and social restrictions were gradually lifted in 2022, demand for Peloton's equipment crashed.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Anthony Di Pizio – Nov 19, 2026 at 5:00PM EST.

10 stocks we like better than Peloton Interactive ›.

According to recent reports, peloton Interactive (PTON -5.23%) stock peaked at around $163 in late 2020, which was a whopping 462% increase from its initial public offering (IPO) price of $29. Consumers were buying the organization's stationary exercise bikes, treadmills, and other equipment hand over fist at the height of the COVID-19 pandemic to maintain their fitness levels at home while gyms were closed.

According to recent reports, but as lockdowns and social restrictions were gradually lifted in 2022, demand for Peloton's equipment crashed. The tech giant promptly found itself in a fight for survival as its losses ballooned into the billions of dollars.

It has been revealed that peloton stock has since plummeted 96% from its peak. However, although equipment sales remain weak, management has made a series of changes to bring the company back from the brink of failure. Here's the good news, the bad news, and whether this might be a buying opportunity for investors.

Peloton's annual revenue peaked at $4 billion in fiscal 2021 (ended June 30, 2021), with equipment sales accounting for $3.1 billion of that total. However, the tech giant's revenue has since declined for five straight years, coming in at $2.4 billion in fiscal 2026 (ended June 30). Equipment sales represented just $770.1 million -- or less than one third -- of the total.

Recent findings suggest that even partnering with third-party retailers like Amazon, Dick's Sporting Goods, and Costco hasn't been enough to revive Peloton's slumping equipment sales. Simply put, the pandemic triggered a unique, one-off spike in demand that the company hasn't been able to replicate, despite its best efforts.

Sources indicate that the bulk of Peloton's revenue now comes from digital subscriptions. There is the connected fitness subscription, which gives equipment owners access to virtual classes and performance tracking tools. Then there is a separate subscription for the tech giant's mobile application, which can be used by fitness enthusiasts who don't own Peloton's equipment. It helps them build workout plans and provides access to certain virtual classes.

Unfortunately, both the connected fitness subscription and the mobile app subscription saw a decline in paying members during the recent fiscal 2027 first quarter (ended Sept. 30), so Peloton is now experiencing a deterioration in sales across both hardware and software.

As a result, Peloton's business is likely to shrink for the seventh straight year, because management is forecasting a 4% decline in revenue during fiscal 2027 overall.

Following Peloton's excellent operating results in fiscal 2021, management positioned the company for more growth by increasing costs. But when that growth failed to arrive in fiscal 2022, Peloton suffered a whopping $2.8 billion net loss at the bottom line, and available cash was quickly running out.

Management proceeded to slash operating costs by 68% between fiscal 2022 and fiscal 2026, and Peloton is now profitable again. It generated a net income of $63.2 million in fiscal 2026, followed by a further $96.2 million in profit during the first quarter of fiscal 2027, after additional cost cuts.

Recent findings suggest that after excluding one-off and noncash expenses like stock-based compensation, Peloton has delivered adjusted (non-GAAP) earnings before interest, taxes, depreciation, and amortization (EBITDA) of $517.7 million over the last four quarters. Simply put, the organization is no longer at risk of going under.

NASDAQ · As of 4:00 PM ET 11/19/26.

If Peloton's revenue continues to decline year after year, the only way it can maintain profitability is by slashing costs even further. But, unfortunately, it will eventually run out of ways to do that -- and every time it pulls money away from areas like marketing, it becomes even harder to generate sales growth. As a result, the company could find itself in a downward spiral in the next few years that will be very challenging to reverse.

According to recent reports, peloton was sitting on over $1.3 billion in cash and cash equivalents as of Sept. 30, so it has some runway to continue testing different strategies to reignite equipment and subscription sales. However, the tech giant is also carrying over $900 million in long-term debt, so it doesn't have an indefinite amount of time to deliver results.

Shrinking businesses tend to destroy shareholder value over time, so I don't think it's a good idea to buy Peloton stock right now, even after its 96% decline. It might be better to wait until the tech giant proves it can deliver consistent revenue growth on an annual basis, because that's the massive missing piece in the turnaround story. Until then, more downside in the stock could be ahead.

With Mortgage Rates Rising, Should You Hibernate Until Spring?

📅 19 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (780 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Nerdwallet

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Mortgage rates are back up this week, wiping out modest relief from a monthlong drop that began in mid-October.
  • The average rate on a 30-year fixed-rate mortgage shot up 29 basis points to 7.28% APR in the week ending Nov.
  • In a recent development, A mortgage is a big ol’ loan, so when rates go up, those fractions of a percentage point add up fast.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Mortgage rates are back up this week, wiping out modest relief from a monthlong drop that began in mid-October.

The average rate on a 30-year fixed-rate mortgage shot up 29 basis points to 7.28% APR in the week ending Nov. 19, according to rates provided to NerdWallet by Zillow. (A basis point is one one-hundredth of a percentage point.) We calculate our weekly average using daily APRs recorded over the past five business days.

In a recent development, A mortgage is a big ol’ loan, so when rates go up, those fractions of a percentage point add up fast. Say you’re borrowing $400,000 on a 30-year fixed-rate mortgage. Compared with last week, your monthly principal and interest payment would be about $78 higher today.

One bad week doesn't make a trend, but a jump like this can make putting your house hunt on hold until spring feel like a safer bet. So … is it?

Before deciding whether to buy a house now or wait, it helps to know what's pushing mortgage rates higher.

Right now, mortgage rates are still feeling the aftershocks from two major inflation reports last week. First, the Consumer Price Index (CPI) indicated consumer prices rose more than expected in October. Then, the Producer Price Index (PPI) showed wholesale inflation climbed 6.5% over the past year — its biggest annual increase in nearly four years.

Sources indicate that while CPI shows how prices have changed, PPI can offer clues about what's coming next. Faced with higher costs, businesses may raise their own prices to compensate, keeping inflation elevated. Federal Reserve policymakers aren't expecting much relief anytime soon, either. According to meeting minutes released Nov. 18, they expect inflation to remain elevated above their 2% target for a while.

Sources indicate that to cool rising prices, the Fed can raise the federal funds rate, which is the benchmark interest rate banks charge each other for overnight loans. The Fed doesn't set mortgage rates, but lenders anticipate its decisions, so mortgage rates often move before the Fed acts. A rate hike is widely expected at the Fed's Dec. 8-9 meeting.

Sources indicate that even after a Fed rate hike, there’s no telling how quickly inflation will cool — or whether mortgage rates will follow. (Inflation is just one of many forces that affect mortgage rates, after all.) So if you do wait until spring to buy a house, don't do it just because you're betting on a cheaper mortgage.

If you're not in a rush to move, winter can be a good time to regroup. Fewer homes typically go up for sale from November through February, so waiting until spring could give you more options.

But upcoming data from the National Association of Realtors suggests this year's slowdown goes beyond the usual seasonal lull. High mortgage rates and home prices are making it tough for many buyers to make the numbers work. For some buyers, waiting isn't a strategy — it's the only option.

Sources indicate that pending home sales, a measure of homes under contract, fell 16.7% in October compared with a year earlier, NAR reports. All four U.S. regions saw declines. At this rate, NAR chief economist Lawrence Yun warned that annual home sales could fall to their lowest level since the mid-1990s.

“Either sizable housing demand is building in the background, or the dream of homeownership is increasingly out of reach for many Americans,” Yun said in a news release.

According to recent reports, whether you're waiting by choice or necessity, you can use the time to strengthen your finances. Paying down debt, strengthening your credit score or saving for a bigger down payment could help you qualify for a better mortgage deal.

Every little bit helps when today’s mortgage rates are this high.

Mortgage preapprovals typically expire after 60 to 90 days. If you're already preapproved, why not keep an eye on listings this winter? (Hey, I’m an optimist. All it takes is one house.).

Think like a seller for a second. If you're listing your house in the dead of winter, you're probably not doing it just for fun. You might have a deadline, and you’re probably more willing to negotiate. In the winter, buyers have less competition — and more room to negotiate a lower price, closing cost credits or repairs. Those savings on the sticker price might help offset today's higher borrowing costs.

Sources indicate that spring typically brings more homes for sale, but it also brings more buyers competing for them. And if mortgage rates end up dropping this spring, you won't be the only one coming out of hibernation.

Further, Broadcom's AI semiconductor business is growing much faster than its higher-margin infrastructure software segments, which could lead to lower gross margins in the medium term. Add that to the fact that investors are still worried about the cyclicality of the semiconductor industry, and it's not too difficult to understand why Broadcom's shares haven't performed well this year.     #50702. AI Agents Will Need A Credit Score For Companies: How Contradictory Records Get Suppliers Dropped From AI Shortlists

    📅 19 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 4m • 📚 Deep Dive (856 w)
    📖 Baca
    AI & Tech ⚠️ Warning 🌐 Forbes ↗ Open Full Page

    AI Agents Will Need A Credit Score For Companies: How Contradictory Records Get Suppliers Dropped From AI Shortlists

    📅 19 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (856 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Forbes

    ⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Joseph Byrum is an accomplished executive leader, innovator and cross-domain strategist with a track record across multiple industries.
    • ​A supplier can be dropped from a buyer’s shortlist by software, and no one at the company will ever know.
    • The AI agent building that list has to decide whether each company is who it claims to be.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Joseph Byrum is an accomplished executive leader, innovator and cross-domain strategist with a track record across multiple industries.

    ​A supplier can be dropped from a buyer’s shortlist by software, and no one at the company will ever know.

    The AI agent building that list has to decide whether each company is who it claims to be. One supplier was acquired last year, and its website carries the fresh name while an official registry still reveals the old one and a public file names a former owner. The agent has no neutral way to settle the conflict, so it moves to the next supplier.

    The company never learns it was evaluated.

    That scene is a projection, and the pieces that would make it routine are being built now.

    Advertising offers a public window; its agent registry and standards are open to inspection and comment. The same logic reaches procurement, where Gartner predicts that by 2028, 90% of B2B buying will be AI agent intermediated, with verifiability a prerequisite.

    Industry observers note that the infrastructure is moving faster than adoption. IAB Tech Lab went from naming its agentic framework to publishing a third-version draft in about seven months, while an IAB survey found the share of U.S. buyers planning more focus on agentic buying fell from 66% to 54% during 2026.

    In a recent development, an agent decides who a company is by comparing what independent sources say about it. When they agree, the match is fast and confident. When they conflict, the agent can guess or move on. In my judgment, a procurement agent has little reason to guess.

    According to recent reports, human buyers already behave this way. McKinsey’s 2026 B2B survey names inconsistent information across a supplier’s teams as the top reason buyers switch suppliers, and ranks generative AI among the top five channels for researching them. I expect an agent to apply the same intolerance for mismatch, only faster.

    The mechanism favors the firm whose name, address and owner read the same everywhere and penalizes the one that changed records in one place only, the normal state after a merger.

    Recent findings suggest that in a recent advisory engagement, a private equity-backed data tech giant acquired a second firm and merged it under its own name. AI systems confused the combined company’s leadership and products, and favored the acquired firm’s descriptions over those of the surviving brand.

    Three conditions combined: By my count, 87% of the independent sources still described the acquired firm, old product and leadership pages stayed live and were never updated, and the acquired firm’s machine-readable records stayed intact and separate, so the systems saw two companies where there was one.

    The name on the door did not decide whose description the systems believed.

    It has been revealed that three groups are building partial checks. IAB Tech Lab’s agent registry checks advertising agents against domain, legal-entity and privacy records. The foundation behind the global tech giant-identification code has published a discussion paper on a credential that lets a counterparty verify who stands behind an agent. Accountants and an AI underwriting firm are rolling out assurance on how agents behave.

    Sources indicate that each system verifies a slice. None verifies the whole.

    Visibility dashboards answer a different question: Is the company mentioned? Because AI answers vary from run to run, a single ranking partly measures noise, and a preprint review of 45 studies notes low source overlap and substantial run-to-run variability in commercial audits. None of it tells a machine whether a company’s facts agree with each other.

    Industry observers note that credit scores settled who to trust with money. Machines will need an answer to whom to trust with a purchase. The shorthand here is an entity authority score, a measure of whether the facts about a organization agree and whether an independent party has checked.

    Three requirements matter most:.

    • Independence: Builders should not grade their own work, and platforms carry a conflict because they would grade their own market.

    • A Range Of Results: The result should arrive as a range, since one run’s number inherits that run’s noise.

    • A Way For Companies To Contest: A wrong score nobody can correct is a shortlist drop with no appeal.

    The inputs are plain: whether official records, app-store accounts and the website agree on name, address and owner, and whether the manufacturer’s own AI agent repeats the public record.

    Recent findings suggest that in my view, some form of entity authority score arrives within one to three years. The best-prepared companies will inventory every place their identity is recorded, from registries and app stores to domains and public files. They will assign an owner to each, correct the mismatches and run an identity check before any acquisition or rename closes.

    The forecast fails if buyers and platforms never require such a check by 2028, or if free platform-verified profiles make a separate score unnecessary.

    The question is whether your tech giant’s records will agree when the first score is computed.

    Forbes Technology is an invitation-only community for world-class CIOs, CTOs and technology executives. Do I qualify?

    As of early evening, Bitcoin (BTC -1.56%) was down 2.15% to $61,635.18, moving dangerously close to the psychologically important $60,000 level. Meanwhile, Ethereum (ETH -1.21%) fell 1.64% to $1,745.57, and Solana (SOL -0.55%) declined 1.56% to $72.47.

    Recent findings suggest that these concerns were compounded by a sharp sell-off on Wall Street, with all three major stock market indexes declining by at least 2%. Gold also fell more than 2%, highlighting the extent of selling pressure across asset classes.

    According to recent reports, perhaps the biggest challenge facing cryptocurrency markets is the absence of sustained buying pressure. Both Bitcoin and Ethereum continue to experience substantial ETF outflows, while Solana's recent return to positive ETF flows has yet to establish a meaningful trend. The persistence of these outflows highlights deteriorating investor demand and the challenges facing the cryptocurrency market as it attempts to establish a bottom.

    With Bitcoin approaching $60,000, investors should be particularly mindful of how the market responds at this level. A decisive break below $60,000 could put additional pressure on the broader cryptocurrency market, particularly as Ethereum and Solana are already struggling to regain lost ground.

    Looking ahead, the prospect of further interest rate hikes and mounting weakness in equity markets make it increasingly difficult to identify a convincing catalyst for a cryptocurrency recovery before year-end.     By Robert Izquierdo – Nov 19, 2026 at 5:33PM EST.

    NASDAQ · As of 4:00 PM ET 11/19/26.

    CoreWeave (CRWV -6.11%), a specialized cloud infrastructure provider, closed at $44.91, down 6.10%. The stock moved after Anthropic priced its IPO above range, which initially lifted AI infrastructure sentiment, resulting in profit taking before concerns over AI costs and rising interest rates ultimately dragged down shares. Investors are watching demand for neocloud capacity and financing costs next.

    Trading volume reached 76.1 million shares, coming in about 63% above its three-month average of 46.5 million shares. CoreWeave IPO'd in 2025 and has grown 12% since going public.

In AI infrastructure and data center services, Nebius Group (NBIS -9.39%) fell 9.39% to $96.92, and IREN (IREN -5.45%) dropped 5.45% to $14.41 as investors weighed neocloud growth and capital needs.

    On Thursday, Nov. 19, Anthropic priced its IPO at $83 a share, above the marketed range, boosting appetite for AI infrastructure names. This helped CoreWeave shares early in the day before profit-taking set in across neocloud stocks.

    CoreWeave initially surged over 9% in morning trading to an intraday high of $52.86, helped by co-founder and Chief Strategy Officer Brian Venturo's announcement that he personally purchased $30 million of CoreWeave's 2031 unsecured bonds.

    It has been revealed that the company posted impressive results for the third quarter. CoreWeave beat Q3 revenue estimates as sales soared by more than $1 billion from Q2, and 168% year over year to $3.7 billion. It also raised 2026 guidance, which remains the clearest fundamental backdrop for the stock's valuation. Earlier this month, CoreWeave stated it targets adjusted profitability in the first half of 2028.

    However, these positives were offset by the manufacturer's ongoing reliance on debt to fuel its AI infrastructure expansion. With inflation remaining persistently high, interest rates are likely to continue moving up. This adds to the cost of CoreWeave's debt payments, with a debt burden exceeding $40 billion at the end of Q3.

    Industry observers note that if the artificial intelligence boom begins to cool, CoreWeave's business could face trouble. That said, the organization signed a multi-year agreement with Anthropic earlier this year to provide AI computing power, and with Anthropic's successful IPO, CoreWeave's prospects may not be as precarious as they seem to some on Wall Street.

    Latest Update: This Oceanfront Hilton Resort in Florida Is Great for Groups
