    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    The fear, when we saw Damian Lillard sitting there with a thousand-yard stare after falling to the ground early in Game 4 of the Milwaukee Bucks' first-round series against the Indiana Pacers in the 2025 NBA playoffs, was that we might never see him again.

    According to recent reports, A ruptured Achilles tendon has altered, if not derailed, plenty of NBA careers. What would it do to a small guard with more than 35,000 NBA minutes on his odometer who was entering his mid-30s?

    What if that — that false step, that unsatisfying whimper of a finish to his time in Milwaukee, an era that felt like an error almost from the moment it started — was the last time we'd ever see Lillard looking like what he'd been for the previous 13 years: among the most dangerous shooters of all time, a generational scoring threat from the second he crossed half-court, one of the 75 greatest players in the league's history?

    An awful lot's happened since then: the shocking waive-and-stretch that ended Lillard's time in Milwaukee (and, more or less, Giannis Antetokounmpo's time there); his subsequent re-signing with the Portland Trail Blazers, the home he never really seemed to want to leave; an entire season spent rehabilitating and recovering, in hopes of giving himself a shot at becoming himself once again.

    (Hayden Hodge/Yahoo Sports Illustration).

    Industry observers note that "All the time off I had, I had to take advantage of it," Lillard recently told NBC. "Not just look at how far out I was and just try to chill or whatever. I had to make sure that every day counted. I was diligent in the process of my rehab, and then when I got back on the court, the weight room, making sure I was balanced on both legs. And then, once it got back to just hooping, that was the easy part — it was just a matter of shaking off the rust.".

    Recent findings suggest that fourteen games into his first action in 18 months, Lillard still hasn't totally shaken it all off and returned to the level that made him a nine-time All-Star and seven-time All-NBA selection. Entering Thursday's matchup against a Bucks team that now looks very different from the one for which he last played, he's averaging 20.1 points, 4.4 assists and 3.0 rebounds in 29.1 minutes per game, and shooting 39.6% from the field — all at or near career lows. He's driving to the basket less frequently than he has since 2013; just 15% of his field goal attempts are coming at the rim, far and away the lowest share of his career. Nearly 60% of his shots, conversely, are coming from 3-point land — by far the largest share of his life in the NBA.

    He's had nights to forget in the early going, like scoring nine points on 3-for-13 shooting in a blowout loss to the Memphis Grizzlies, or finishing with nine on 2-for-15 shooting in Monday's loss to the Minnesota Timberwolves. Those two single-digit performances, by the way, are already as many as Dame has had in any whole season since 2014.

    In a recent development, dame's also had moments to remember, though. Like dropping 25 points with a half-dozen 3-pointers in 24 minutes on the Phoenix Suns in Portland's season opener, his first live action in 543 days ….

    … or knocking down a side-step dagger in the right corner to hand the Los Angeles Lakers one of just three losses they've suffered on the season ….

    … or punctuating a 13-point third quarter against the Oklahoma City Thunder with a vintage, swashbuckling just-inside-the-logo buzzer-beating pull-up triple over the outstretched arms of 7-foot-3 rookie Aday Mara:.

    Recent findings suggest that "I knew he was gonna shoot," Blazers two-way guard Chris Youngblood told Conor Bergin of Blazer's Edge after the win over OKC. "I was like, 'If this goes in, this crowd is about to go crazy.'".

    Even amid the fits-and-starts with his finishing, Lillard has helped give Portland fans plenty to go crazy about in a pleasantly surprising start to the season — one in which he's been a lot more than just a nice story.

    Recent findings suggest that the Blazers enter Thursday at 9-5, in sixth place in the Western Conference, with the NBA's No. 8 offense and No. 10 defense, according to Cleaning the Glass. (The last time the Blazers ended a season in the top 10 on both ends of the floor: 2014-15.) They've taken down Luka Dončić's Lakers in L.A. and Nikola Jokić's Nuggets in Denver, swept a two-game baseball series from Shai Gilgeous-Alexander's Thunder at Moda Center, and looked like a team capable of building on last season's return to the playoffs, ownership misadventures and personnel shuffling be damned.

    Dame's done it in part by working his way into a new normal — one in which he's no longer the sun around whom the entire organization orbits, but rather one component of a constellation in which All-Star forward Deni Avdija often shines brightest.

    Sources indicate that heading into the season, one of the main questions hanging over the Blazers was how first-year head coach Micah Nori would craft an offensive ecosystem that kept everything copacetic despite introducing two decorated All-Star on-ball playmakers (a returning Lillard, an incoming Ja Morant) alongside Avdija, who rose to prominence and helped return Portland to the postseason by becoming the league's highest-volume driver and establishing new career highs in usage, shot attempts, touches and time of possession. The early returns were positive: The Blazers are plus-19 in 66 minutes with Avdija, Lillard and Morant sharing the floor, scoring a scorching 125.9 points per 100 possessions in their minutes with both Dame and Ja taking a smaller slice of the total offensive pie.

    The overarching experiment got paused when Morant went down with a hamstring strain, leading Nori to shuffle his starting lineup — first by sliding fourth-year guard Scoot Henderson into Morant's spot, and then, with Scoot struggling, swapping in 6-foot-6 forward Sidy Cissoko for a bigger, more defensively sound look. Portland's allowing just 106.5 points-per-100 with Cissoko on the court alongside ace defensive center Donovan Clingan and swingman Toumani Camara — a near-best-in-the-league level of point prevention.

    According to recent reports, removing one ball-handler from the mix has somewhat reduced the need for offensive sacrifice, but Lillard has continued to keep up his end of the bargain. He is finishing 27.7% of Portland's offensive possessions with a shot attempt, foul drawn or turnover — his lowest usage rate since 2014-15, when he was setting up LaMarcus Aldridge. His on-ball percentage — literally the share of his floor time that he has the ball in his hands — is the second-lowest of his career.

    Dame has never averaged fewer touches or a lower time of possession, spent less time operating in the pick-and-roll, or spent more time lurking as a catch-and-shoot option. Just under 19% of the offensive possessions Lillard has finished this season have come while spotting up away from the primary action, according to Synergy Sports Technology's tracking data — more than twice as much as in 2022-23, the final year of his first stint in the Pacific Northwest.

    "Being on this team and having less responsibility than I had before, I don't have to make every play," Lillard told Sean Highkin of the Rose Garden Report. "I don't have to score every basket. I just came into this season mostly focused on how I could impact winning. I know that at the end of games, I'm gonna have to make shots and make plays and make free throws. But over the course of a game, I think the load is just lighter.".

    Deploying Lillard as a different sort of threat in a smaller-scale role has proven useful to the overall offensive operation for the Blazers, who are scoring like a top-five offense with Dame on the floor — and like a near-top-10 unit when he's on the floor without Avdija, which were minutes in which Portland's offense died last season.

    Last season, even with Avdija ascending as a downhill menace, primary playmaker and point-producing weapon, the Blazers finished the season just 20th in offensive efficiency, due partly to struggles with ball security (dead last in the NBA in offensive turnover rate, with 90 more live-ball turnovers than any other team in the league), shot-making (27th in team 3-point accuracy, 29th from midrange, 21st in overall effective field goal percentage) and half-court execution (just 29th in points per half-court possession). The arrival of Lillard has helped: Portland has turned the ball over less frequently, generated a higher share of its shots from 3-point land, shot better in the midrange, and scored more efficiently in the half-court with Dame on the floor this season.

    Even with Lillard not quite at the peak of his shot-making powers, his presence opens things up for the rest of the offense. With him on the floor, nearly 53% of Avdija's 2-point baskets have come via assist — 20 percentage points higher than when Dame sits. The driving lanes that were so often so congested last season are open a bit wider with defenses needing to account for Lillard, who ranks eighth in the NBA's gravity metric — a stat aiming to quantify "how much a player pulls defenders towards them [...] how much attention they draw compared to what the spacing on the floor predicts" — just south of one high-volume superstar scorer in a ball-handling timeshare (Donovan Mitchell) and two designated sharpshooters playing off high-usage primary creators (Klay Thompson, Duncan Robinson).

    It has been revealed that that company feels illustrative of the space Lillard at the moment finds himself occupying: not peripheral, still vital, but more of a complement than a centerpiece. (He still can shift into primary mode, though; on Tuesday, with Avdija sidelined by a sore left foot, Dame scored a team-high 25 points with five assists against the Timberwolves, pushing the NBA's No. 1 defense to the brink in a game that Portland nearly, and perhaps should have, won.).

    In a recent development, plenty of superstars over the years have struggled to find comfort moving into that space. Perhaps due to the time away, though, Lillard seems to be navigating the shift fairly smoothly.

    According to recent reports, "Obviously, for the sake of rhythm and timing, you want to be on the ball sometimes, which I am," Lillard recently told Sam Amick of The Athletic. "But I think it just lessens the load of having to sometimes beat two guys, or get into the paint and do too much when we've got so many guys that can do that. I can space the floor, give guys space, and also catch and attack on the second side. It's been a process, kind of finding the spots, and it's becoming more natural. But it's been great as far as how I feel physically, how I'm able to play late in games, the effort and energy I'm able to give defensively throughout games. And I think it's a more sustainable way for us to handle the game.".

    Eighteen months ago, we wondered if we'd ever see Dame look like Dame again. While the jury's still out on that, what he's been so far — in terms of his combination of scoring and shooting efficiency, and by metrics like win shares per 48 minutes, box plus-minus, value over replacement player and player efficiency rating — nets out to something like a top-20 guard in the league. Just a month after coming back from one of the most devastating injuries an NBA player can suffer, that's not nothing … and, with a little more time, a little bit of luck and a lot more hard work, it's also not where Lillard's return is going to stop.

    It has been revealed that "This early in the season, I still feel like I'm getting it back completely — just that rhythm, and taking bumps, and moving at the pace of the league," Lillard told NBC. "But I'm feeling better and better. [...] I've just got to keep it rolling, and keep doing what I'm doing.".

    • By Prosper Junior Bakiny – Nov 19, 2026 at 6:45PM EST.
    • Last year, Johnson & Johnson (JNJ -2.04%) acquired a smaller biotech, Halda Therapeutics, in a cash transaction valued at $3.05 billion.
    • Industry observers note that JNJ-6143 is part of an experimental class of cancer medicines called Regulated Induced Proximity Targeting Chimera, which use proteins found in cancer cells to disrupt certain functions those cells need to survive.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    By Prosper Junior Bakiny – Nov 19, 2026 at 6:45PM EST.

    10 stocks we like better than Johnson & Johnson ›.

    Last year, Johnson & Johnson (JNJ -2.04%) acquired a smaller biotech, Halda Therapeutics, in a cash transaction valued at $3.05 billion. The key asset from that transaction was JNJ-6143, an investigational, early stage candidate for prostate cancer. It will take time to determine whether this acquisition was worth it for Johnson & Johnson, but recent clinical developments suggest that the $3.05 billion the pharmaceutical giant spent may have been well spent. Let me explain.

    Industry observers note that JNJ-6143 is part of an experimental class of cancer medicines called Regulated Induced Proximity Targeting Chimera, which use proteins found in cancer cells to disrupt certain functions those cells need to survive. This approach could lead to much stronger efficacy than existing standards of care for certain cancers. Johnson & Johnson's JNJ-6143 showed the potential of these therapies in a Phase 1 clinical trial, the results of which it presented at the European Society for Medical Oncology 2026 Congress, held in Madrid in October.

    Sources indicate that the medicine was tested in patients with metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer. Notably, these patients had received a median of four prior therapies, so we aren't dealing with an easy-to-treat cancer. Yet, JNJ-6143 performed extremely well. It led to an overall response rate (the percentage of patients who respond to treatment) of 75% among patients with measurable disease. This data is highly encouraging. Of course, this was only an early stage study. There is a long road ahead before JNJ-6143 earns approval, that is, if it performs well in future clinical studies.

    NYSE · As of 4:00 PM ET 11/19/26.

    Industry observers note that however, this once again highlights the strength of Johnson & Johnson's pipeline. The tech giant has successfully expanded its lineup of approved drugs in recent years, with newer introduces such as Imaavy, which treats generalized myasthenia gravis, and Icotyde, a therapy for plaque psoriasis.

    Sources indicate that these newer launches could help the company overcome headwinds, such as government-led drug price negotiations and patent cliffs, that it will face over the medium term. Over the next five years, Johnson & Johnson should make significant progress across its pipeline, including with JNJ-6143. Johnson & Johnson's innovative abilities are one of the key reasons the stock is attractive.

    And it's worth noting that the manufacturer's innovative medicines division could perform even better over the long run, given that it has spun off its slower-growing consumer health division and can focus more on its higher-growth pharmaceutical business. Johnson & Johnson's medtech unit adds even more depth and diversification to the business.

    It has been revealed that finally, Johnson & Johnson remains one of the best dividend stocks on the market. With its streak of 64 consecutive years of payout increases, the healthcare leader is a Dividend King, or a stock with 50 or more straight annual dividend increases. Income seekers should stick with this stock for the long term.

    Investors looking beyond the short-term noise and focusing on long-term returns can track top Wall Street analysts to pick the right stocks, backed by strong research.

    Here are three stocks favored by some of Wall Street's top pros, according to TipRanks, a platform that ranks analysts based on their past performance.

    In a recent development, this week's first stock pick is Datadog, an AI-powered observability and security platform. The organization will announce its results for the third quarter on Nov. 4. Datadog is seeing strong demand for its offerings, thanks to cloud migration and rapid AI adoption. TipRanks' KPIs tool for DDOG reveals the growth in its customer base over the past few years amid increasing market penetration and growing adoption of its products.

    In a recent development, heading into Q3 FY26 earnings, Bank of America analyst Koji Ikeda reiterated a buy rating on Datadog stock and raised his price target to $335 from $305. The analyst noted that industry checks and data indicate that infrastructure software demand is strengthening, with AI increasingly driving usage and growth.

    Ikeda called Datadog and Atlassian his top picks, saying that companies that can show that AI is a tailwind to growth could see their valuation rerate, even at premium multiples. He added that the total addressable market for observability is growing faster than anticipated, driven by accelerated growth of enterprise AI and the rapid ramp of consumer AI agents.

    It has been revealed that the five-star analyst believes that focus will be on revenue growth, which he estimates to be 28.7% for Q3 FY26 versus the Street's consensus of 29.1%. Ikeda thinks that the market is underestimating the growth prospects of DDOG's security products. Meanwhile, he cautioned investors about concentration risk related to large customers.

    "We think results will be supportive of our long-term thesis that Datadog is a strong share gainer in the rapidly expanding observability opportunity," mentioned Ikeda.

    Ikeda ranks No. 673 among more than 12,500 analysts tracked by TipRanks. His ratings have been successful 55% of the time, delivering an average return of 10.9%. See Datadog Statistics on TipRanks.

    Sources indicate that the next pick, semiconductor giant Nvidia, is also benefiting from AI-driven demand for its products. After attending Nvidia's GTC Berlin conference, Morgan Stanley analyst Joseph Moore reaffirmed a buy rating on NVDA stock with a price target of $300, calling it a top pick in the semiconductor space.

    In a recent development, the five-star analyst said that the conference supported his thesis that Nvidia continues to effectively navigate bottlenecks in the supply chain, land/power/shell, and funding. In fact, Moore is "convinced that all 3 aspects are opportunities for NVDA.".

    While Nvidia's GTC Berlin offered no major updates, Moore noted the conference reflected that the firm continues to add to its significant advantages heading into 2027. The analyst mentioned that Vera Rubin is gaining momentum, though details on next year's Rubin Ultra were lighter than expected.

    With demand outpacing supply, Moore said that focus is on closing the gap. In this regard, he highlighted the supply chain deals on substrate, packaging and testing. While the analyst continues to view TSMC 3 nm wafer supply as the biggest challenge, he expects it to ease over time.

    Moore ranks No. 142 among more than 12,500 analysts tracked by TipRanks. His ratings have been profitable 59% of the time, delivering an average return of 23.4%. See Nvidia Ownership Structure on TipRanks.

    Aerospace organization SpaceX recently declared solid third-quarter results, with its AI revenue surging to $7.56 billion from $813 million in the prior-year quarter.

    Impressed by the results, Needham analyst Ryan Koontz reiterated a buy rating on SPCX stock with a price target of $250. Koontz highlighted that SpaceX's Q3 results significantly exceeded expectations, proving that the company's vertically integrated business model is driving massive scale.

    It has been revealed that furthermore, Koontz emphasized the 195.2% sequential growth in SpaceX's AI revenue, fueled by wholesale spot compute deals. He noted management's increasing focus on its AI strategy, given that it is optimistic about adding 10 gigawatts of incremental capacity during 2027.

    "With increasing confidence on Starship re-use, we meaningfully increase our estimates," said Koontz.

    Koontz ranks No. 357 among more than 12,500 analysts tracked by TipRanks. His ratings have been profitable 42% of the time, delivering an average return of 23.7%. See SpaceX Technical Analysis on TipRanks.

    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Democrats' midterm election win has put the artificial intelligence trade in question, as voters clearly expressed opposition to the rapid buildout of data centers.
    • In this scenario, investors can add dividend-paying stocks to their portfolios to earn steady income.
    • Here are three dividend-paying stocks that are highlighted by Wall Street's top pros, as tracked by TipRanks, a platform that ranks analysts based on their past performance.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Democrats' midterm election win has put the artificial intelligence trade in question, as voters clearly expressed opposition to the rapid buildout of data centers. The stock market could remain volatile amid AI trade concerns, macro uncertainties, and geopolitical tensions.

    In this scenario, investors can add dividend-paying stocks to their portfolios to earn steady income. However, the extensive universe of dividend stocks can make selection challenging. Top Wall Street analysts' recommendations can help investors shortlist attractive dividend stocks, as these experts assign ratings after in-depth financial analysis.

    Here are three dividend-paying stocks that are highlighted by Wall Street's top pros, as tracked by TipRanks, a platform that ranks analysts based on their past performance.

    Recent findings suggest that viper Energy (VNOM) is a subsidiary of Diamondback and owns and acquires mineral and royalty interests, primarily in the Permian Basin. The company reported upbeat third-quarter earnings, supported by recent acquisitions and continued development activity from Diamondback and third-party operators. Viper announced a base cash dividend of 50 cents per share for Q3 2026, payable on Nov. 19. Based on the base and variable dividends announced over the past 12 months, VNOM's dividend yield stands at 5.7%.

    Following the Q3 results, TD Cowen analyst Aaron Bilkoski reiterated a buy rating on Viper Energy stock with a price target of $61. The analyst noted that the company delivered solid Q3 results, with production, including oil and natural gas liquids, exceeding both TD Cowen and consensus estimates.

    The 5-star analyst highlighted that the key update was the announcement of two royalty acquisitions for $809 million in cash, including deferred consideration, and $82 million of newly issued shares.

    Given the recently unveiled base dividend hike, Bilkoski expects Viper to direct incremental free cash flow toward buybacks. While the acquisitions increase leverage, the analyst believes that Viper has enough capacity for opportunistic buybacks.

    According to recent reports, bilkoski noted that Viper has historically delivered one of the highest production per share growth profiles in his royalty coverage, but still trades at a notable discount to the royalty peer average and the company's historical FCF yield range. "In our view, its above-average growth warrants a higher valuation," said the analyst.

    Bilkoski ranks No. 525 among more than 12,500 analysts tracked by TipRanks. His ratings have been profitable 57% of the time, delivering an average return of 12.80%. See Viper Energy Stock Buybacks on TipRanks.

    Exxon Mobil (XOM) reported robust Q3 2026 profits, as its U.S. refineries boosted production to capitalize on the high diesel fuel prices sparked by the conflict in the Middle East. The oil and gas giant declared a quarterly dividend of $1.07 per share, payable on Dec. 10, reflecting a 3.9% increase. This marks Exxon's 44th consecutive year of dividend increases. At an annualized dividend of $4.28 per share, XOM offers a yield of 2.53%.

    Impressed by the Q3 print, TD Cowen analyst Jason Gabelman reiterated a buy rating on Exxon stock and raised his price target to $193 from $180 to reflect higher downstream earnings, with the expectation of increased mid-cycle margins.

    Recent findings suggest that gabelman noted that the strength in Exxon's refining business continues to offset Middle East-related headwinds. He added that the company increased its ownership in LNG projects, which should reduce its Middle East concentration over time from 75% to 50% and lower the likelihood of diversification-focused mergers and acquisitions. Beyond LNG, Gabelman expects Exxon's growth in the 2030s to come from Guyana, Kashagan, Permian, and possibly Venezuela.

    Gabelman noted that Exxon announced a dividend hike of nearly 4% and plans to maintain buybacks at $20 billion for 2027. "The decision to maintain reduces the pro-cyclicality nature of the buyback," said the analyst.

    According to recent reports, gabelman ranks No. 347 among more than 12,500 analysts tracked by TipRanks. His ratings have been successful 66% of the time, delivering an average return of 16.90%. See Exxon Mobil Ownership Structure on TipRanks.

    Williams (WMB), which owns and operates energy infrastructure to deliver natural gas, reported strong third-quarter results. The firm revealed a quarterly dividend of $0.525 per share, or $2.10 per share annualized, payable on Dec. 28. WMB offers a dividend yield of 3.09%.

    Industry observers note that in reaction to the Q3 2026 results, CIBC analyst Robert Catellier reaffirmed a buy rating on Williams stock with a price target of $82. The analyst noted that Q3 results were essentially in line with expectations and reflected continued strength in execution across WMB's infrastructure portfolio.

    Catellier mentioned that Williams' Q3 performance was driven by higher transmission, storage, and power generation revenues, as well as contributions from the Momentum Midstream acquisition.

    According to recent reports, he noted that Williams maintained its full-year EBITDA guidance of $8.3 billion to $8.5 billion. In fact, results are tracking toward the higher end of the guidance range, backed by contributions from recently completed projects and the Momentum Midstream deal. WMB continues to target long-term EBITDA compound annual growth rate of at least 11% through 2030.

    Catellier expects WMB's long-term targets to be supported by incremental transmission and storage opportunities, including Transco's Southeast Supply Enhancement II project and an 84 MMcf/d expansion of the Garden Connector project.

    Recent findings suggest that catellier ranks No. 667 among more than 12,500 analysts tracked by TipRanks. His ratings have been successful 66% of the time, delivering an average return of 9.60%. See Williams Technical Analysis on TipRanks.

Co-founder and President Alex Eu, my longtime business partner, remains the principal operating officer and decision-maker for Teamshares on operations matters. We would really love to thank our colleague, Madhuri, for her years of service at the company. She has made a great impact, having joined the company in its earliest days in 2021 when we had just four companies.

    It has been revealed that as a broader note, we are grateful to all the colleagues at the operating companies and at the parent company, all aligned with shareholders and growth. We are equally grateful to the investors and creditors who back Teamshares on its growth journey. Separately, we are attending a number of upcoming investor conferences, including one of the Roth conferences on Wednesday. You can see those all listed on our IR website, and Mike would love to hear from you. With that, it is back to the salt mines to finish up a strong rest of the year, and we look forward to seeing you in March.

    Operator: Thank you all for participating in today's conference. You may now disconnect.

    #50614. Fantasy Basketball Rookie Report: Tiered rankings for top 1st-year players one month into the 2026-27 NBA season

    📖 Baca
    General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Yahoo ↗ Open Full Page

    Fantasy Basketball Rookie Report: Tiered rankings for top 1st-year players one month into the 2026-27 NBA season

    📅 19 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 6 min read (1283 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Yahoo

    ⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Recent findings suggest that rookies are usually a patience game, but this class is producing in November.
    • According to recent reports, the two formats reward different strengths: efficiency and balanced contributions matter more in 9-cat, while volume drives points-league value.
    • Here's the first rookie report of the 2026-27 season.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Recent findings suggest that rookies are usually a patience game, but this class is producing in November. To compare their value across formats, I averaged each rookie's Yahoo Fantasy 9-cat and standard points ranks into a composite. Both rankings are league-wide, not rookie-only, so a rank of 66 means 66th in fantasy value — not 66th among rookies.

    According to recent reports, the two formats reward different strengths: efficiency and balanced contributions matter more in 9-cat, while volume drives points-league value. The composite offers a snapshot across both, while the gap between ranks indicates which format suits each player best. I also included true shooting percentage, which accounts for 3s and free throws to give a fuller picture of scoring efficiency than field goal percentage alone.

    Here's the first rookie report of the 2026-27 season.

    Sources indicate that boozer is the best rookie in the class by composite (40.5) and in 9-cat (47th), and his 34th ranking in points is only behind Darius Acuff Jr. among rookies. He's at 9.4 boards and 5.3 assists with 16.6 points in 31.1 minutes, and that kind of massive-man passing is rare, especially for a first-year player. The 40% shooting is the one number holding him back, but 88.9% from the line and 1.9 3s a game lift his true shooting to 53.5%. His 14.1% rebound rate is the highest of any rookie on this list.

    It has been revealed that I touted Bulls F Caleb Wilson as the player with the highest ceiling, but Boozer looks like he could be right there as a consistent double-double threat with the added bonus of high-end playmaking for fantasy managers. A cool record that he's pacing toward: he'd be the first rookie forward to average 15-10-5, and only the second rookie to do it since the "Substantial O" Oscar Robertson in 1960-61.

    It has been revealed that lendeborg is right behind Boozer, ranking 42nd in points and 87th in 9-cat for a 64.5 composite as one of the most complete rookies in the class. He's at 20.8 points on 46.4% shooting with 7.3 rebounds, 3.5 assists and 1.1 steals, and his 26.4% usage rate indicates Golden State is running things through him. His 58.1% true shooting is the best of the five rookies who use at least 24% of their team's possessions. He gets to the line nearly six times a game, so there's a floor even when the shot isn't falling. With Stephen Curry out, expect Yaxel to build on his early-season success as the primary engine of Golden State's offense.

    Everyone in this tier is shooting under 42%, but their true shooting sits around 53%, so the damage is smaller than it looks. The question is what each one gives you while the shot comes around. For Acuff, it's points, assists and 3s: 26.0 points, 7.0 assists and 3.3 3s in 36.7 minutes, with a 32.5% usage rate that is like a veteran's workload. Despite his ball-hog persona, he's assisted on 34.2% of his teammates' baskets while on the floor — the highest rate of any rookie and 15th in the NBA. The price is 41% shooting on 22.6 attempts (52.9% true shooting) with 3.9 turnovers and limited stocks. Even with that, he's 88th in 9-cat, which is a strong result for a rookie shooting this poorly and reveals how much his counting stats carry him. In points leagues, he's 24th, so he's a top-30 player there and a clear starter across formats.

    In a recent development, wilson is out 4-6 weeks with a right metacarpal fracture, but his 10 games before the injury were strong: 18.9 points, 6.2 rebounds, 1.8 steals, 0.9 blocks and 2.3 3s in 30.8 minutes. That scoring-stocks-and-boards profile is the hardest to find amongst this specific rookie class. If Norman Powell gets traded (his contract is movable), Wilson would become Chicago's primary scorer. Combine that with his versatility and he'd be a player well worth trading for and stashing on IL.

    Sources indicate that peterson's route to fantasy prominence is through scoring, assists and 3s. It's happening sooner than expected, as his opportunity share is expanding with injuries to Lauri Markkanen and Jaren Jackson Jr. It's left him as Utah's second scoring option, with a chance to be the primary one until they return. He's at 16.5 points, 2.2 3s, and 1.1 steals in 30.6 minutes and he shoots 84.0% from the line. He also protects the ball better than the other high-usage rookies in the top two tiers, with a turnover rate of 10.4 per 100 possessions, compared to 13.0 to 16.9 for the rest. Peterson's sporting a 29.2% usage rate with Markkanen off the floor (19.9% with him), so a natural jump in production will push Peterson into a top-100 asset in 9-cat and top-75 in points pretty swiftly.

    Thomas is the most efficient scorer in this tier, with 13.4 points, 2.6 3s and 1.2 steals in 23.9 minutes on 47.5% shooting. The second-rounder has been one of the Cavs' best weapons off the bench, connecting on 44% of his 3s, while 54% of his shots come from beyond the arc. He's seeing a healthy 21% usage rate but only turns it over 1.2 times a game. There aren't many ways for him to hurt you, which explains why he's the highest-ranked rookie in this tier in 9-cat. He's a good add in 12-team leagues.

    Aday Mara is picking up steam, averaging 12.5 points, 7.7 rebounds, 3.0 assists and 1.5 blocks in 26.5 minutes over his last six games while shooting 68% from the field. He's scored in double figures in all six contests, raising his season averages to 9.2 points, 6.5 boards and 1.7 blocks. The recent production makes him worth a look for fantasy managers seeking rebounds, blocks and a field-goal percentage boost, though his 57.7% shooting from the line remains a drawback. At 50% rostered, shallow league managers should consider him, especially given Isaiah Hartenstein's injury history.

    Dybantsa is the most interesting gap in the class: 216th in 9-cat and 85th in points. He's playing heavy minutes (33.8 per night), and at 16.3 points, 6.6 rebounds, 2.3 dimes and 1.3 steals per game, the volume is there. What's missing is efficiency, at 41.6% from the field and 71.9% from the line, which hurts a 9-cat build far more than it does in points leagues. That's more of a shooting problem than a role problem, so I'd buy him now in points leagues and be more patient in 9-cat.

    It has been revealed that wagler's main fantasy value comes at the free-throw line and 3s, where he shoots 85.9% on 5.5 attempts per game while averaging 12.5 points overall. The 37.0% shooting is an issue, and he's not providing much beyond scoring (6 combined rebounds and assists per game). However, it's a long season and the Clippers will likely increase his minutes and usage as the season progresses.

    These four are 12-team options to keep on your watchlist or get a jump on before your leaguemates do.

    Lendeborg and Boozer claim the top spots one month into the season, with Acuff's counting stats pushing him into the top tier. He is, after all, the best points-league rookie by a wide margin. Peterson and Mara's growing roles give them upside, and Dybantsa is one of my trade targets for points leagues. Be on the lookout for Flemings now that CJ McCollum will miss four weeks, and the more the Bucks lose, the more Burries' minutes will increase as the season goes on.

    Sources indicate that I'll upgrade this report monthly as roles and production settle. Until then, prioritize steady minutes and production over draft pedigree.

    Tokenization platform Securitize gains 10% postmarket on Q3 results, move into asset-backed finance

    📅 09 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 2 min read (437 words, 📖 Standard) | Source: CNBC

    ⏱️ ~2 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Tokenization platform Securitize climbed about 10% postmarket after reporting third quarter growth alongside increased operating expenses, and announcing an expansion into asset-backed finance through a strategic acquisition.
    • In a recent development, miami-based Securitize, which made its public market debut in July, operates in the relatively fresh corner of the crypto equity universe involved in institutional tokenization infrastructure.
    • The growth came as bullish sentiment around tokenization gained traction throughout the third quarter, ahead of the Security and Exchange Commission formalizing the long awaited Innovation Exemption on Sept.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Tokenization platform Securitize climbed about 10% postmarket after reporting third quarter growth alongside increased operating expenses, and announcing an expansion into asset-backed finance through a strategic acquisition.

    In a recent development, miami-based Securitize, which made its public market debut in July, operates in the relatively fresh corner of the crypto equity universe involved in institutional tokenization infrastructure. Tokenized assets on the platform grew 9% in the third quarter, to $4.8 billion, from the same period a year ago. Aggregate transaction volume rose 20% from a year ago, to $4.3 billion. Revenue of $11.5 million was up 28% from last year.

    The growth came as bullish sentiment around tokenization gained traction throughout the third quarter, ahead of the Security and Exchange Commission formalizing the long awaited Innovation Exemption on Sept. 17, which created a temporary pathway for trading of certain tokenized stocks and strengthened the regulatory outlook.

    Profitability is still meaningfully below year-ago levels, due in part to costs associated with going public over the summer, as well as the scaling up of the tokenization business at an active time for the entire sector, Securitize CEO Carlos Domingo told CNBC in an exclusive interview.

    Securitize reinforced "certain areas of the company like finance, compliance, legal [and] cybersecurity," which increased corporate costs "compared to a year ago when we were privately held," Domingo noted. "We're in in a very good position. The adjusted EBITDA … is improving significantly from previous quarters.".

    Securitize reported an adjusted EBITDA loss of $2 million, compared with positive adjusted EBITDA of $3.6 million a year ago, better than a $5.5 million loss in the second quarter. The company posted a 183% increase in operating costs and expenses.

    Also on Monday, the Securitize board authorized a $50 million share buyback and announced the acquisition of River One, an institutional asset-backed financing platform developing technology to connect stablecoin capital with traditional lending markets. Terms were not disclosed.

    Securitize sees an opportunity to modernize the $9 trillion market for asset backed finance by using stablecoins to finance real world assets, generate yield and tokenize investment positions and credit products, Domingo said.The acquisition also marks an expansion beyond Securitize's core niche markets at a time when tokenization's competitive landscape is growing, with traditional asset managers like BlackRock and Franklin Templeton, and established financial market infrastructure providers like DTCC and Broadridge, entering the industry.

    "We have been very active in tokenized funds, treasuries [and] yield … And we've been obviously recently very active in tokenized stocks, so this adds another piece of the puzzle in the emerging tokenization space for us to capture revenue growth.".

    📅 20 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 2 min read (313 words, 📖 Standard) | Source: Fool

    ⏱️ ~2 mins left to finish

    💡 Key Takeaways
    • By Kailey Hagen, CFP® – Nov 19, 2026 at 7:00PM EST.
    • Spousal Social Security checks tend to be a lot smaller than retirement benefits, averaging just $988 in October 2026 compared to $2,092 for retirement checks.
    • Spousal benefits have a few rules that make them different from retirement benefits, and it's key to understand them if you plan to apply for these checks next year.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    By Kailey Hagen, CFP® – Nov 19, 2026 at 7:00PM EST.

    Spousal Social Security checks tend to be a lot smaller than retirement benefits, averaging just $988 in October 2026 compared to $2,092 for retirement checks. But they can still make a meaningful difference to your household's budget in 2027.

    Spousal benefits have a few rules that make them different from retirement benefits, and it's key to understand them if you plan to apply for these checks next year. Here are three of the biggest differences you should be aware of.

    It has been revealed that it's crucial that you and your spouse are both on the same page about when each of you will apply so that you can maximize your household income. If you haven't already talked through your aims, now is a great time to do so before you try to apply for Social Security benefits in 2027.

    Spousal benefits are also available to ex-spouses if you were married to a qualifying worker for at least 10 years before divorcing and you haven’t remarried. Your ex's remarriage will not affect your eligibility to claim benefits on the ex's work record.

    In a recent development, social Security retirement benefits continue to grow for every month you delay your application until you qualify for your maximum checks at age 70. But spousal benefits only grow until you reach your full retirement age (FRA). This is 67 if you were born in 1960 or later.

    #50593. Industry News: What's ahead for AI financing after Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang departs

    📅 13 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 4m • 📚 Deep Dive (751 w)
    📖 Baca
    AI & Tech ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 CNBC ↗ Open Full Page

    Industry News: What's ahead for AI financing after Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang departs

    📅 13 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (751 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: CNBC

    ⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang's departure hasn't produced a broad shock to the credit market, but it is putting the company's role as a financier of artificial intelligence infrastructure under scrutiny.
    • Huang, who stepped down Thursday amid an espionage and adultery scandal, built Nvidia into an AI powerhouse in the 33 years since he co-founded the manufacturer.
    • In a recent development, nvidia not only supplies its graphics processing units to hyperscalers and tech giants, it also provides financing to other companies to help the industry expand.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang's departure hasn't produced a broad shock to the credit market, but it is putting the company's role as a financier of artificial intelligence infrastructure under scrutiny.

    Huang, who stepped down Thursday amid an espionage and adultery scandal, built Nvidia into an AI powerhouse in the 33 years since he co-founded the manufacturer. Chief financial officer Colette Kress has been named interim CEO as the company searches for a permanent chief executive.

    In a recent development, nvidia not only supplies its graphics processing units to hyperscalers and tech giants, it also provides financing to other companies to help the industry expand. That could all change.

    "Although we expect the organization to fulfill all of its previously declared commitments, we believe that going forward, it may be more difficult for the company to negotiate newly introduced multi-party investments among ecosystem partners at the same scale it has done up to this point," Goldman Sachs analyst James Schneider stated in a note Thursday.

    The news of Huang's resignation comes after investors were already concerned about the massive amount of debt being taken on to fund AI infrastructure.

    In a recent development, tech bond yields have risen and spreads have widened on credit default swaps, most notably in lower-rated names. Credit default swaps are contracts in which investors pay for protection in case the borrower can't repay its debt. Wider spreads indicate investors view the bonds as riskier.

    Sources indicate that on Friday, the yield on Nvidia's 4.5% bond due in 2031 sat at 5.717%, nearly 5% higher week to date. Bond yields move inversely to prices.

    Tech stocks slumped Friday with the Nasdaq 100 closing down 1.2% as markets continued to digest the Nvidia news. Yields on hyperscaler bonds ticked slightly higher on Friday, signaling the broader concern about AI debt lingers.

    According to recent reports, it's the smaller AI companies that could ultimately see an impact if Nvidia makes any changes to its AI financing. The firm had $36 billion in off-balance-sheet AI cloud agreements, or backstops, for neoclouds, according to its last quarterly financial filing in July.

    Neoclouds CoreWeave, Nebius and IREN are all in Nvidia's portfolio. Their shares were down sharply Thursday.

    According to recent reports, coreWeave, which has become the poster child for AI debt fears, saw its bond yields retreat after its quarterly earnings on Tuesday eased investor concerns. The yield on its 9.75% bond due in 2031 was 14.79% on Friday after climbing to 16.7% last week. The spread on its five-year CDS also dropped more than 17% week to date, although it remained above 1,000 — which is generally considered a sign of distress.

    It remains unclear how Nvidia's support for those companies may change, said CreditSights analyst Andy Li.

    "We don't know what the ultimate strategy for Nvidia is going to be coming out the other side," he mentioned.

    "However, I think directionally, just given the fact that Jensen was so crucial in selling the Nvidia story and being a very aggressive deal maker, it's likely that a lot of this creative deal-making and circular financing and equity and credit support is going to moderate," he added.

    CoreWeave CEO Michael Intrator told CNBC Wednesday, before Huang's departure, that Nvidia "is not one person.".

    Sources indicate that "There are thousands of people over there that interface with thousands of people at my tech giant every day. They integrate on the technology. They integrate on the physical infrastructure. They integrate on the networking," he noted in an interview with "Squawk on the Street." "They have been a great partner for us for years. They will continue to be a great partner for us.".

    It has been revealed that bob Lang, founder and chief strategist at Explosive Options, doesn't see any major changes in terms of Nvidia's relevance or its ability to finance for now. As CFO, Kress was involved in the financing deals, and the search for a permanent CEO is going to take some time, he noted.

    The real problem is just how much money the company will want to lend for AI financing, rather than, say using its hundreds of billions in free cash flow for other purposes, like share buybacks, capex, or acquisitions.

    "Significant companies like Nvidia and Meta, they're holding all the cards," he said. "When they decide that the game is over, that's it — it's going to be curtains for some of these smaller companies.".

    — CNBC'S Kif Leswing and Isabel O'Brien contributed reporting.

    💡 Key Takeaways
    • President Donald Trump met with Vladimir Putin and Xi Jinping individually on Thursday, ahead of a scheduled trilateral with his Russian and Chinese counterparts, according to pool notes and Chinese state media.
    • On greeting the Russian president on the sidelines of the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation forum, Trump said he had a "great relationship" with Putin, adding they had known each other for a long time and expressed hope that "a lot of wonderful things can come out of this, or at least start.".
    • The two presidents were meeting for the first time since a summit in Alaska in August last year.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    SHENZHEN, China — U.S. President Donald Trump met with Vladimir Putin and Xi Jinping individually on Thursday, ahead of a scheduled trilateral with his Russian and Chinese counterparts, according to pool notes and Chinese state media.

    On greeting the Russian president on the sidelines of the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation forum, Trump said he had a "great relationship" with Putin, adding they had known each other for a long time and expressed hope that "a lot of wonderful things can come out of this, or at least start.".

    The two presidents were meeting for the first time since a summit in Alaska in August last year.

    Russian presidential aide Yuri Ushakov said the talks lasted for approximately 40 minutes, and Putin left the meeting place in "an excellent mood," according to Russian state news outlet Ria Novosti.

    Russia's full-scale invasion of Ukraine was a key topic for the talks, Ushakov remarked, alongside preparations for the trilateral summit with China's Xi.

    In a separate bilateral meeting, Trump said he had discussed the Ukraine war with Xi, saying they should work together to bring an end to it.

    "We're looking to both help with respect to the war with Russia and Ukraine," Trump said, according to Reuters. "I'd like to see it ended," he added.

    Xi, meanwhile, said the two countries should cooperate to prevent artificial intelligence safety risks and strengthen communication on trade, according to Chinese state media.

    Recent findings suggest that earlier on Thursday, the leaders and other members of APEC gathered for a summit. Trump and Xi entered the room side by side.

    Xi noted China would provide $20 million to support APEC cooperation, and establish a "Center for Asia-Pacific Community Studies in Shenzhen to conduct policy research and exchanges and provide intellectual support.".

    Later in the morning session, Trump noted that he opposed regulating artificial intelligence as it would "stifle" the industry.

    "The United States has been a Pacific power for hundreds of years, and we continue to work to promote growth and stability, sovereignty, prosperity, and peace throughout this region," Trump stated.

    U.S. officials said last week that Trump did not blueprint to raise Nvidia's Jensen Huang and allegations of an affair with a Chinese spy at his meetings.

    Trump holds talks separately with Putin and Xi ahead of their historic trilateral meeting.

    Takaichi gets chilly reception in China on first Japan leader visit since 2019.

    Trump arrives in China for historic meeting with Xi, Putin.

    China's Xi calls for removing trade and investment barriers.

    Three things to watch as Trump, Xi and Putin meet in China.

    "The scale of China's economic strength and technological ambition is clear to U.S. businesses," he said. "They recognize the importance of the Chinese market, but also understand that they need to remain competitive, innovative, and prepared to compete in an increasingly sophisticated business environment.".

    #50573. Latest Update: Musk accuses Zelenskyy of lying about Starshield restrictions in Ukraine

    📅 19 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 3m • 📚 Deep Dive (538 w)
    📖 Baca
    General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 CNBC ↗ Open Full Page

    Latest Update: Musk accuses Zelenskyy of lying about Starshield restrictions in Ukraine

    📅 19 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (538 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: CNBC

    ⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • SpaceX founder Elon Musk accused Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy of being untruthful about restrictions around Ukraine's Starshield network and said Kyiv wanted to use Starlink for offensive operations.
    • Asked at The Newly introduced York Times' Dealbook Summit about Zelenskyy's claims that Starshield had been slowed down, Musk said, "That's false ...
    • When pressed on whether he meant Ukraine was not always truthful, Musk doubled down with a reply: "No, it's not always truthful.".
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    SpaceX founder Elon Musk accused Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy of being untruthful about restrictions around Ukraine's Starshield network and said Kyiv wanted to use Starlink for offensive operations.

    Asked at The Newly introduced York Times' Dealbook Summit about Zelenskyy's claims that Starshield had been slowed down, Musk said, "That's false ... I don't want to blow your mind, but Zelenskyy is not always truthful.".

    When pressed on whether he meant Ukraine was not always truthful, Musk doubled down with a reply: "No, it's not always truthful.".

    Recent findings suggest that his comments came after Zelenskyy on Wednesday noted speed restrictions remained in place on Starshield, hampering Ukraine's ability to intercept Russian missile and drone strikes. "We are discussing this with the American side," he said.

    It has been revealed that russia invaded Ukraine in February 2022, stoking a conflict that has resulted in a refugee crisis and hundreds of thousands of deaths. Ukraine has been able to beat back Russian forces more effectively than many observers thought possible, despite having a much smaller land area and population.

    However, it relies heavily on SpaceX's Starlink and Starshield for capabilities like battlefield communications and drone operations. Musk has previously said that "if we were to turn off Starlink, the entire Ukrainian front would collapse immediately.".

    In a recent development, the SpaceX CEO sought to distinguish between Starlink, a commercial satellite network, and Starshield, a military system developed by SpaceX and operated by the U.S. government.

    Musk said that Starlink is subject to speed limits because it is not intended for offensive military operations, adding that such missions should instead use the Starshield network.

    Sources indicate that "Any action taken by Starshield is up to the War Department. Starlink is commercial and is not intended as a weapon of war," Musk noted, referring to the U.S. Department of Defense.

    In October, Musk said the U.S. government and President Donald Trump were responsible for any restrictions on Ukraine's Starshield network after slowdowns to the service were reported.

    It has been revealed that "Starshield systems are owned and controlled by the U.S. government. Any limits on speed or usage are decided by the US military and ultimately POTUS," Musk wrote on X.

    The Wall Street Journal later reported on Oct. 20 that Musk had ordered the slowdown, citing U.S. officials and people familiar with the matter.

    "What I'm trying to tell you is Zelenskyy is actually asking to use the Starlink commercial satellites for events of military actions, and we have declined to do so, as we have declined to do so from the beginning of this conflict," Musk added in the interview.

    It has been revealed that on Oct. 24, Musk mentioned SpaceX had restricted Ukraine's access to Starlink because Kyiv had violated the service's terms by using it for offensive drone strikes, a claim Ukrainian officials disputed.

    "Ukraine military violated Starlink terms of service and used it for offensive drone strikes to kill people. That loophole was closed last week," Musk wrote on X one day after.

    Industry observers note that CNBC has reached out to Ukraine's ministry of foreign affairs for comment but did not receive a response. The president's office could not immediately be reached.

    It has been revealed that family offices increased their allocation to public stocks to 36.4% of their portfolios in the third quarter, up from 35.6% in the second quarter, according to the Tracker. Their stock holdings have jumped from 33.6% in 2024, a substantial increase for family offices, which rarely deviate from their long-term financial allocations.

    According to recent reports, the CNBC Family Office Portfolio Tracker is powered by data from Addepar, the foundational data and artificial intelligence platform used by financial professionals globally that now has over $10 trillion on its platform. Unlike surveys, Addepar's data provides a real-time look into the portfolios of hundreds of single-family offices — aggregated and anonymized —representing a total of more than $1.4 trillion in family office assets.

    The increased allocation to stocks, whether from passive market gains or active buying, indicates that family offices aren't pulling back from the market despite growing fears of an AI bubble and weakness in tech stocks.

    "As we've studied family offices for more than 15 years, they've demonstrated time and again that they take the long view," said Eric Poirier, CEO of Addepar. "But they do like staying invested. So with the run-up in AI thematically, they're staying exposed, they're risk on.".

    At the same time, family offices are hedging their tech bets. According to Addepar, family offices have lower exposure to AI stocks when compared to the broader S&P 500. While tech stocks account for 40% of the S&P market cap, family offices have an average allocation of 28% of their equity portfolios in tech stocks, according to the Tracker.

    They are offsetting the tech risk in part with financials. Financial services account for 11% of the S&P, but the average allocation for family offices is 18%. Poirier said the lower tech weighting and higher financials exposure suggests that family offices see financials as a potential offset to AI risk.

    "They're fading the AI trade to some extent, but still staying quite exposed," he said.

    Family offices are also continuing to dial back their exposure to alternative investments. Alts account for 47% of their portfolios, down from 48.5% a year ago. The biggest decliner was real estate, down to 7.2% from 9.4% in the third quarter of 2025. Higher interest rates have driven down valuations in many real-estate portfolios and funds, likely accounting for much of the drop.

    Hedge funds also saw a decline, from 8.9% a year ago to 7.5%, as many funds grapple with more volatile stock markets and declining tech stocks. Their investments in private credit declined slightly, to 1% of their portfolios. Their private equity holdings fell for the second straight quarter, to 6.4% of their portfolios.

    It has been revealed that they also saw a decline in their allocation to private companies — companies held directly rather than through a private equity fund. Family office holdings of private companies fell 0.3% to 15.7%, likely due to slight declines in valuations. Still, private companies remain by far their largest segment among alts, as family offices continue to focus on direct investing.

    Cash piles grew slightly for family offices — to 8.6% — suggesting they want to keep adequate dry powder on hand in case of a market correction or crisis.

    According to recent reports, the significant question for family offices this year and next is how they manage rising yields and inflation fears. Some were positioning for inflation at the start of the year with bets on infrastructure and real estate, yet the surge in the yields driven by oil prices was faster than many expected.

    Family office holdings of fixed income have steadily increased for three straight quarters, to 8.1% in the third quarter.

    In a recent development, "Family offices tend to be able to withstand market volatility more so than other investors," Poirier mentioned. "That said, their response to the historic rise in fixed income and rates has been more muted relative to even five-year averages.".

    The Inside Wealth newsletter by Robert Frank is your weekly guide to high-net-worth investors and the industries that serve them.

    Is a bottom in for the Nasdaq-100? Charts to watch

    📅 13 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (579 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: CNBC

    ⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • (See the video above for Frank's complete chart breakdown.).
    • Is the Nasdaq-100's recent bounce a sign that the bottom is in?
    • First, let's remember how we got here.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    (See the video above for Frank's complete chart breakdown.).

    Is the Nasdaq-100's recent bounce a sign that the bottom is in? We're going to look at several charts to help answer that question.

    First, let's remember how we got here. In September, the NDX broke out from a bullish cup-and-handle pattern, producing a 33,200-upside target. That breakout rapidly failed, however, and gave way to a bearish pattern that broke down aggressively two weeks ago.

    The decline brought the index relatively close to its 26,350 downside target before the current rebound began.

    It has been revealed that zooming out, it's telling to see where the bounce originated. Three important forms of support converged in the 25,000-26,000 area:.

    This confluence of support helped encourage buying after a roughly 15% decline.

    For perspective, we also see what larger drawdowns of 20%, 30%, 40%, and 50% would look like … a lot worse.

    The following chart tracks NDX drawdowns from 52-week highs going back to just after the financial crisis. Only a handful of declines exceeded 20%, and three produced relatively quick reversals: late 2018, the Covid lows in 2020 and April 2025.

    Historically, buying into declines of approximately 15%–25% has generally paid off, even when additional downside occurred first (yellow highlights).

    The chart also highlights previous declines of 10%–16% in green, putting the current pullback into perspective.

    The major exception was 2022, when the NDX eventually declined nearly 36% over approximately 10 months ... a much worse outcome, which many investors are concerned could happen again now.

    That raises the key question: Are we experiencing another routine correction, or the early stages of a larger bear market?

    One crucial clue will be how far this bounce progresses.

    It has been revealed that any rally that fails to reclaim the previous highs could establish a significant lower high. Additional lower highs would provide stronger evidence of a developing, longer downtrend.

    We saw this in March 2022, when that first sharp rebound effort failed to reach the previous high before a much more severe decline followed.

    The bottom line: The current bounce is encouraging, particularly given where it originated and knowing how well buying prior 10-20% drawdowns has paid off.

    It has been revealed that from here, it's all about the follow through. We don't need to see latest highs right away, but any rally from here that's met with another wave of strong selling could reignite downside momentum.

    #50560. Latest Update: Takaichi gets chilly reception in China on first Japan leader visit since 2019

    📅 19 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 3m • 📚 Deep Dive (683 w)
    📖 Baca
    Business & Policy ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 CNBC ↗ Open Full Page

    Latest Update: Takaichi gets chilly reception in China on first Japan leader visit since 2019

    📅 19 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (683 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: CNBC

    ⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Japanese Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi received a subdued welcome on her first trip to China as premier, signaling Beijing's limited appetite for repairing ties strained by a simmering row over Taiwan.
    • At gatherings such as this week's Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation summit in Shenzhen, protocol details — including who greets a visiting leader at the airport and where they are positioned in official photographs — often convey political messages.
    • Takaichi was met on the tarmac Wednesday by a retired Chinese diplomat, rather than a serving official, and Japan's ambassador to China, Kenji Kanasugi.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Japanese Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi received a subdued welcome on her first trip to China as premier, signaling Beijing's limited appetite for repairing ties strained by a simmering row over Taiwan.

    At gatherings such as this week's Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation summit in Shenzhen, protocol details — including who greets a visiting leader at the airport and where they are positioned in official photographs — often convey political messages.

    Takaichi was met on the tarmac Wednesday by a retired Chinese diplomat, rather than a serving official, and Japan's ambassador to China, Kenji Kanasugi.

    Industry observers note that the low-key reception contrasted sharply with the warmer welcomes given to other visiting leaders, including South Korean President Lee Jae Myung, while U.S. President Donald Trump was greeted personally by Chinese President Xi Jinping.

    In the leaders' group photo, Takaichi was placed in the back row, off to the side and several places from Xi, who stood alongside Trump and Russian President Vladimir Putin.

    "Beijing sought to downgrade her official status to that of a head of government rather than a head of state," said Jeremy Chan, senior analyst at Eurasia Group.

    During Thursday morning's greeting line, Takaichi spent several minutes trying to talk to the Chinese leader without an interpreter present, while most leaders exchanged handshakes and kept walking.

    "It has become increasingly difficult for her to engage in formal or even informal conversations with Xi," stated Kei Koga, an associate professor at Nanyang Technological University in Singapore, who sees Takaichi's intention as to still "project the image that she could still communicate with him despite the ongoing tensions.".

    At a press briefing Thursday afternoon, Takaichi said Japan's position on Taiwan remained unchanged as stated in the 1972 Japan-China Communique, adding that her leadership has been communicating with Chinese counterparts on rare earth export controls.

    Takaichi's subdued reception signaled Beijing's lack of enthusiasm to repair ties with Tokyo, analysts remarked, potentially prolonging China's curbs on critical mineral exports that have gripped Japanese industries for the past year.

    "China's frosty reception of Takaichi reveals quite clearly that Beijing is not yet ready to forgive her over her remarks about Taiwan," Chan noted, expecting the bilateral relationship to remain strained until Takaichi leaves office.

    That could leave Japan grappling with continued restrictions on rare earth supplies from China next year, mentioned Tianchen Xu, senior economist at the Economist Intelligence Unit.

    Relations deteriorated sharply after Takaichi noted in November 2025 that a Taiwan Strait crisis could constitute a situation threatening Japan's survival and warrant a self-defense response.

    While the substance broadly aligned with Japan's existing security policy, previous prime ministers had generally avoided stating it so explicitly in a Taiwan scenario.

    China reacted angrily and demanded that Takaichi retract the remarks. She has not done so, while stating that the door to dialogue with Beijing remains open, with minimal high-level contact over the past year.

    According to recent reports, china has since tightened restrictions affecting Japan, including controls on dual-use and rare earth exports with potential military uses. It also discouraged its citizens from traveling to Japan and halted Japanese seafood imports.

    Takaichi's visit marked the first trip to China by a Japanese prime minister since Shinzo Abe traveled to Chengdu in December 2019 for a trilateral summit with Chinese and South Korean leaders.

    No formal Takaichi-Xi meeting has been publicly scheduled during her visit. Meanwhile, Xi is expected to join Trump and Putin for a historic trilateral gathering on Thursday, alongside a bilateral meeting with Trump.

    Takaichi needs to show a "reflection of what she said about Taiwan a year ago," said Huiyao Wang, founder of the Beijing-based Center for China and Globalization, which is often seen as close to Beijing's thinking.

    Wang remarked Tokyo should show greater flexibility, pointing to Trump's comments that the U.S. would avoid getting involved in the Taiwan matter. He argued that Japan holding firm on the issue would not help relations with Beijing.

    Such reflection, he stated, "would really help to clarify some of those misunderstandings between the two countries.".

    — CNBC's Evelyn Cheng contributed to this report.

    #50555. Intel signs first external customer for advanced 18A chips

    📅 19 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 2m • 📖 Standard (496 w)
    📖 Baca
    Hardware & Chips ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 CNBC ↗ Open Full Page

    Intel signs first external customer for advanced 18A chips

    📅 19 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 2 min read (496 words, 📖 Standard) | Source: CNBC

    ⏱️ ~2 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Intel CEO Lip-Bu Tan said on Wednesday that the company has signed the first outside customer for its 18A chips.
    • It has been revealed that "Resilient supply on the foundry is very notable," Tan remarked at the TomorrowX Summit in Austin, Texas.
    • Sources indicate that it's a milestone moment for Intel in its five-year effort to take on chip manufacturing leader Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Co.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Intel CEO Lip-Bu Tan said on Wednesday that the company has signed the first outside customer for its 18A chips.

    It has been revealed that "Resilient supply on the foundry is very notable," Tan remarked at the TomorrowX Summit in Austin, Texas. "And then 18A, I'm involved in production and we just signed the first customer," Tan added, without naming the debut client.

    Sources indicate that it's a milestone moment for Intel in its five-year effort to take on chip manufacturing leader Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Co. After years of missteps and low yields, Intel touted 18A as key to a turnaround that would finally convert the company into a competitive chip manufacturer for non-Intel products.

    "It's a huge win for foundry," Creative Strategies analyst Ben Bajarin told CNBC in an interview.

    It has been revealed that pushkar Ranade, Intel's technology chief, clarified on X that the external customer had signed up for Intel's 18A-P manufacturing process node, which went into risk production in June. In May, reports indicated that Apple and Intel were closing in on a deal to use Intel's foundry to make some of the chips for Apple devices.

    Intel's stock has lost more than half its value since the end of September, with most of that plunge coming late last month after the firm noted revenue this quarter will be at least $1 billion shy of analysts' estimates due to a PC sales slump and supply chain challenges.

    In considering who the customer may be, Bajarin pointed to Nvidia, Apple or the major hyperscalers that make their own custom processors.

    "Amazon, Microsoft and Google are struggling to get capacity for their CPU ambitions at TSMC," he said. "So it makes sense that you go somewhere for at least some capacity.".

    Tan mentioned in late October that he sees the global market for server processors increasing as much as five times over the next five years to about $200 billion, but that Intel can't presently meet customer demand.

    Sources indicate that wall Street has turned on Intel of late after the chipmaker had become a top trade starting in the middle of last year. The U.S. government took a 10% stake in Intel in August 2025, and Nvidia followed with a $5 billion investment, as optimism grew around the prospect of U.S.-made chips that could replace an almost complete reliance on Taiwan.

    Until now, Intel has had no marquee customer for its foundry business, primarily manufacturing chips for its own products at its factories, including a huge new campus in Arizona.

    Intel is a leader in another step of the chipmaking process known as advanced packaging, where individual chips are packaged together and connected to the larger system. Tan also unveiled on Wednesday that Microsoft is its first publicly named customer for its most advanced packaging technology, known as EMIB.

    —CNBC's Kif Leswing contributed to this report.
